articles.title: Ex-NFL Star Antonio Brown Appears in Miami Court but Judge Delays Hearing on Expected Plea Deal
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown's court hearing where he was expected to accept a plea deal and avoid prison time in an attempted murder case was postponed Wednesday.
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star wide receiver Antonio Brown's court hearing where he was expected to accept a plea deal and avoid prison time in an attempted murder case was postponed Wednesday.

Brown arrived in a Miami courtroom Wednesday morning and was ready to plead no contest to aggravated assault and be sentenced to probation, his lawyer said. But a Florida judge said she was in the middle of another trial and not ready to go forward. The hearing was pushed back to Oct. 28.

Brown is accused of grabbing a handgun from a security staffer after a celebrity boxing match in Miami on May 16, 2025, and firing two shots at a man he had been in a fistfight with earlier, according to an arrest warrant. Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu told investigators one of the bullets grazed his neck.

Defense attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown was looking forward to putting the case behind him. Eiglarsh said the plea deal offered by prosecutors was too good to turn down and that it says Brown would not be considered a convicted felon.

"It's a setback because it's another month that my client has an ankle monitor on and doesn't have closure, which everybody in this case wants," Eiglarsh said. He said he was "cautiously optimistic" the judge would agree to the terms.

Brown could face up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge. He has said on social media that he was defending himself from an attack and others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Florida's Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Nantambu said after Wednesday's postponement that he hopes Brown will take advantage of the deal to "become a better person and be there for his family."

"We want him to get the healing that he needs," he said.

Richard Cooper, an attorney for Nantambu, said Nantambu forgave Brown and would not cooperate with law enforcement.

At one point in the court's hallway, Brown slipped on a dark mask while talking to his attorney and then pulled it off before going into the hearing.

Brown, 38, spent 12 years in the NFL and was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in the 2021-22 season for Tampa Bay and won a Super Bowl with quarterback Tom Brady the previous season.

Over the course of his career, much of it spent with Pittsburgh, he had 928 receptions for more than 12,000 yards and accounted for 88 total touchdowns, including punt returns and one pass.

During a January 2022 game with Tampa Bay against the New York Jets, Brown took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field, leading to his release by the Buccaneers and effectively ending his career.

Brown has dealt with several legal problems over the years. He previously was accused of battery of a moving truck driver , several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai , where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer promises to improve as Jerry Jones flags Cowboys’ gaffes in late loss to Ravens in Brazil
articles.summary: Jerry Jones expressed deep frustration over the Dallas Cowboys' final 28 seconds against the Baltimore Ravens, saying no explanation is satisfying.
articles.body: Longtime Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did little to hide his frustration with how the final seconds unfolded in Sunday’s improbable loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL’s debut game in Rio de Janeiro. After Dallas scored to tie the game at 31 in the final minute, Baltimore received the ensuing kickoff with just seven seconds remaining. The game appeared destined for overtime. Instead, Brandon Aubrey’s kickoff sailed into the end zone for a touchback, and Lamar Jackson’s 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers moved the Ravens into position for a game-winning field goal. Jones and Schottenheimer retraced the offensive sequence that culminated in Brandon Aubrey’s 23-yard game-tying field goal, beginning with the playcalling after Dallas reached first-and-goal at the 2-yard line. They also examined Prescott’s third-down throwaway, which forced the Cowboys to settle for the tying kick. Jones acknowledged that the Cowboys could not change what happened in the final seconds but said they could use the experience to avoid repeating the same mistakes. "There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," the longtime Cowboys general manager said during his latest appearance on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan. JERRY JONES ISSUES 'DANGEROUS' WARNING AFTER COWBOYS TOPPLE COMMANDERS BEHIND DAK PRESCOTT'S HISTORIC DAY "Let's be sure that we all understand that. [The coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with. ... But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again. You can't get that back. [There's] no way to get it back. What you can do is use it ... to get better. That's what's being done." Schottenheimer struck a similar tone in his first public comments since the Cowboys returned to the U.S., acknowledging the mistakes, accepting responsibility and emphasizing his continued alignment with Jones. Great, sound advice. I value him. He's been around the game a long time, just like I have, and he's seen a lot of stuff. "And so to me, that shows that he and I are aligned very closely. This will make me better. I'll be better. And again, I'm looking forward to lining up and playing this week against the Texans." Schottenheimer then turned the focus to his own performance, adding, "I hurt our chance to win that game and I'll be better. And I'm better than that. Schottenheimer, the son of former NFL coach Marty Schottenheimer, said frustration over the third-down call influenced the kickoff decision, while communication between special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen and game management coordinator Ryan Feder also fell short. "My dad had a rule — one play at a time," he said. "He talked a lot about it, because it happened to him. He made a decision on a play, it didn't go good, he was pissed off about it and it affected another decision. I think that's kind of what happened to me. So I'll take accountability for it. It's football and life. It's what happens." Schottenheimer is just 20 games into his head-coaching career after spending a quarter-century on various NFL coaching staffs. articles.title: B/R's Week 4 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: Time flies when you're having fun—or when you're driving yourself crazy. Either way works.
articles.body:
Time flies when you're having fun—or when you're driving yourself crazy. Either way works.

The first month of the 2026 fantasy football season is winding to a close. For some, it has been a bonanza of breakouts.

For others, it has been one problem after another. Injuries have already ravaged the roster. Healthy players aren't living up to their draft-day price tag. The losses are piling up.

However, whether you are 3-0 and rolling or 0-3 and reeling, we all have one thing in common: Everyone wants to get a win in Week 4.

As always, this column aims to assist fantasy managers in that endeavor with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start and sit calls, and some Week 4 sleepers.

It's a one-stop shop of fantasy football goodness.

We're changing the format for this week's rankings. Instead of presenting the list position by position, we're using a sortable, searchable tool packed with valuable information.

As always, there are no quarterbacks listed in the overall rankings (which can be useful when making "flex" decisions). If you play in a "superflex" league and have a viable second QB, he should be in that spot.

Case Keenum now being on that list for the Bears is the 2026 season in a nutshell.

We expected Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills to be an elite fantasy option this season, and while he cooled off a bit in Week 3, he still leads the position in fantasy points .

However, Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers was drafted in most leagues as a borderline starter, and he leads all NFC signal-callers in fantasy points through three weeks.

If Purdy has been a pleasant surprise, Bryce Young of the Carolina Panthers and Tyler Shough of the New Orleans Saints have been stunners.

Young and Shough were late-round afterthoughts at best. Now, after three games the former is averaging 313 passing yards per game, while the latter has posted three straight outings with over 20 fantasy points.

Baker Mayfield of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is the latest quarterback to go down this season. He's expected to miss at least a few games after dislocating his thumb in last week's loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Drake Maye of the New England Patriots was the fourth quarterback drafted on average over the summer. Now, after a turnover-plagued start in which he has yet to post even 10 fantasy points in a game, the third-year pro ranks outside the top 30.

This week's London game between the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders doesn't appear all that appealing to fantasy managers at first. But there could be some aerial fireworks Sunday—both teams possess bottom-three pass defenses.

Bryce Young, Carolina Panthers (vs. Detroit Lions)

Young's production slowed last week after a torrid start to the season, but he should kick right back into high gear in Week 4. The Panthers are going to have to throw to keep up with the Lions, and Detroit's defense has been non-existent so far this season.

Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns (vs. Pittsburgh Steelers)

Don't look now, but Watson has quietly been a top-10 fantasy quarterback through three games in 2026. Look elsewhere if you need a Week 4 spot-starter, though. The Steelers have surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to QBs this season.

Case Keenum, Chicago Bears (vs. New York Jets)

Keenum was fantastic last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, accounting for three touchdowns and finishing inside the top five in fantasy points. He's firmly on the streaming radar with Caleb Williams expected to miss at least a couple more games.

Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was the first overall pick in more fantasy leagues than not this year.

He's living up to that price tag—and then some.

Three games into the season, Gibbs is the highest-scoring fantasy running back by a wide margin, averaging a ridiculous 32.8 PPR points per game. Last week against the New York Jets, Gibbs piled up 164 total yards, caught seven passes and found the end zone three times.

The fourth-year pro is averaging over 150 total yards and a pair of touchdowns per game.

When De'Von Achane went down with a torn ACL last week, second-year pro Ollie Gordon II took over as the Miami Dolphins' featured back. However, his fantasy outlook remains limited. Miami's offensive struggles cap his upside, and Jaylen Wright 's potential return from a stinger and foot injuries could create a committee that limits Gordon's workload.

Achane wasn't the only big-name back who went down in Week 3— Breece Hall of the New York Jets has been labeled "week to week" with a thigh injury suffered in Detroit. Braelon Allen will be in the low-end RB2 conversation for as long as Hall is out, including this week in Chicago.

A miserable start to his tenure with the New Orleans Saints has become even worse for Travis Etienne Jr . He injured his hamstring in last week's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders and is expected to miss time. The Saints were already struggling to run the ball, so it's hard to get excited about the prospects of Alvin Kamara or Kendre Miller while Etienne is sidelined.

Bucky Irving, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (vs. Green Bay Packers)

The good news is that after sitting out most of the fourth quarter last week with an undisclosed ailment, Irving is expected to be fine for Week 4. The better news is that Tampa will lean on the run with Jalon Daniels under center against a Green Bay Packers defense that was just gashed on the ground by the Atlanta Falcons.

Omarion Hampton, Los Angeles Chargers (at Seattle Seahawks)

The Chargers have been abysmal offensively so far this season, and that funk has spread to Hampton, who ranks outside the top-20 in PPR points after three weeks. Don't expect things to improve this week in Seattle—the Seahawks have allowed just 87 yards per game on the ground this season.

Rachaad White, Washington Commanders (vs. Indianapolis Colts)

White had just 41 scrimmage yards last week against Seattle, but he found the end zone and snuck into the top-20 backs in PPR points for the week. He will make it three straight games with double-digit PPR points this week in London against a Colts team allowing the sixth-most PPR points to running backs this year.

Three games into the 2026 campaign, the highest-scoring player in fantasy football isn't a quarterback like Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, or a running back like Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions.

At this point in the season, we are living under the benevolent reign of King Jaxon I.

Seattle Seahawks wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba has been on an absolute tear to start the season. The reigning Offensive Player of the Year leads the NFL with 27 receptions, 405 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns.

Smith-Njigba is on pace to record 156 receptions for 2,295 yards and 32 touchdowns. All three would shatter NFL records.

Oh, and he's averaging just under 35 PPR points per game.

After a massive Week 1, the fantasy production of Justin Jefferson of the Minnesota Vikings has tailed off, although he still ranks inside the top-15 at the position for the year. Now the shaky quarterback play in Minnesota isn't the biggest hurdle Jefferson faces—he suffered a low-ankle sprain last week against the Buccaneers and is questionable for Week 4.

Raise your hand if you had Kalif Raymond of the Chicago Bears pegged as a top-12 fantasy option entering the season. Now put your hand down—lying is wrong. After reeling in six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown against the Eagles, Raymond is second on the Bears in targets and leads the team in receptions and receiving yards.

There are any number of injuries to monitor at wide receiver. Mike Evans of the San Francisco 49ers is likely out this week after injuring his ribs in Week 3. Nico Collins of the Houston Texans has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury but could return in Week 4. Jalen Coker of the Carolina Panthers injured his quad against the Cleveland Browns. And Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams is expected to miss a third straight contest with a groin injury.

Josh Downs, Indianapolis Colts (vs. Washington Commanders)

Downs has yet to find the end zone, but after five catches for 77 yards last week he has 12 PPR points in back-to-back weeks. His best game of the season is coming Sunday against a Washington Commanders secondary allowing almost 47 PPR points per game to wide receivers in 2026.

Ladd McConkey, Los Angeles Chargers (at Seattle Seahawks)

This isn't piling on the Chargers offense. OK, maybe it is. The truth is that the Bolts have struggled to get anything going this year, and Sunday they face an angry Seahawks defense that has given up the fourth-fewest PPR points to wide receivers this year.

Mack Hollins, New England Patriots (at Buffalo Bills)

In last week's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Hollins led the Patriots in targets (9), receptions (6), and receiving yards (87). The Buffalo Bills remain undefeated, but their pass defense has been vulnerable early in the season, ranking 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game.

It was a massive gut punch for fantasy managers when the Raiders tight end had knee surgery just before the season began. That procedure caused the third-year pro to miss the first two games of the season.

Bowers was back out there Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, and he picked up where the folks who drafted him early over the summer expected—13 targets, 10 catches, 116 yards and a touchdown.

Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals has some company in the top tier of tight ends now.

Travis Kelce of the Kansas City Chiefs had a down season by his standards in 2025, but even in that "down" year he was still quietly third in PPR points among tight ends. It's still early, but he appears to have turned back the clock in 2026. The 36-year-old is averaging over 16 yards a catch and is on pace for his first 1,000-yard season since 2022.

Kelce isn't the only aging tight end who has started the season strong. George Kittle of the San Francisco 49ers looks fully recovered from the Achilles injury he suffered in last year's playoffs. The 32-year-old was the NFC's highest-scoring tight end in Week 3 after posting six catches, 82 yards and two scores against Arizona.

At this rate, Kyle Pitts of the Atlanta Falcons may not catch six passes for 82 yards all season long. As a matter of fact, fantasy football's No. 2 tight end only has six targets through three games. He has parlayed those targets into a whopping two catches for 20 yards and 1.3 PPR points per game.

Darren Waller, Carolina Panthers (vs. Detroit Lions)

After scoring a pair of touchdowns in Week 2, Waller led the Panthers in targets and catches in last week's loss to the Cleveland Browns. This week Waller faces a Detroit Lions team that leads the league in PPR points allowed to tight ends, and with Jalen Coker (quad) iffy at best Waller should see a solid target share again in Week 4.

Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills (vs. New England Patriots)

Kincaid is off to an excellent start to the season—even after a down Week 3 he's still inside the top five in PPR points at the position. A second straight clunker could be in the offing Sunday against the New England Patriots—the Pats are allowing just 6.2 PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars (at Cincinnati Bengals)

With just seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown for the season, Strange's fourth professional season is off to a quiet start. He'll get louder on Sunday in the Queen City. For whatever reason, the Bengals have been a sieve against opposing tight ends for years, and 2026 hasn't been any different.

At 3-0, they may well be the biggest surprise of the first three weeks of the 2026 season, and the Raiders defense has played a part in that success.

Last year, Vegas finished the season 25th in the NFL in points allowed. This year, the Raiders are eighth in that regard at 18 points per contest.

Vegas has been producing for fantasy managers as well. Thanks to the fourth-most sacks in the league and an NFL-high nine takeaways, the Raiders lead all AFC defenses in fantasy points and are the only team in the NFL to post double-digit fantasy points in all three outings this season.

This week's matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs is easily the Raiders' most difficult matchup to date, but the team's defensive improvement has been impressive.

The Minnesota Vikings are on quite the rip so far this season—they have improved from a fantasy perspective every week, culminating in six sacks, two interceptions and a defensive score last week against Tampa. With Brian Flores running an ultra-aggressive scheme and a dream matchup this week with the disappointing Dolphins, the Vikings are the top defensive play in Week 4.

In 2025, the Houston Texans were the No. 1 defense in the NFL in yards allowed and second in fantasy points. They were one of the first defenses drafted in 2026, but it has been a slow start to the season—Houston sits 12th in fantasy points after three games. A matchup with the high-octane offense of the Dallas Cowboys isn't going to help.

If the Texans have been mildly disappointing to this point in the season, the Philadelphia Eagles have been a flat-out bust. Drafted fifth on average among defenses over the summer, the Eagles have struggled to generate big plays despite two favorable matchups in three games and have the fifth-fewest fantasy points at the position.

Jacksonville Jaguars Defense (at Cincinnati Bengals)

The Jaguars have been dominant defensively in their two home games this season but stumbled in the second half at Denver in Week 2. Jacksonville will regain its road-warrior footing this week in Cincinnati against a Bengals team allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to defenses in 2026.

Philadelphia Eagles (vs. Los Angeles Rams)

The Rams have actually been kind to opposing defenses this season—or at least they were a bonanza for the Broncos last Sunday night in Denver. But the Eagles just cannot generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks, and if you give Matthew Stafford time he will absolutely pick you apart.

Green Bay Packers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Green Bay's defense was a Week 3 dud against Atlanta, and the run defense was especially poor. Still, the Packers have an inviting bounce-back matchup in Week 4: Tampa Bay ranks 27th in total offense, has allowed the most fantasy points to opposing defenses and is expected to turn to an undrafted rookie at quarterback.

Want proof of why drafting a fantasy kicker before the last round is a terrible idea? Check out the leaderboard at the position after three weeks.

Of the top five kickers in 2026 (well, six—there's a tie for fifth place), just two (Tampa's Chase McLaughlin and Kansas City's Harrison Butker ) were drafted inside the top 12. The others were largely undrafted or late-round options.

Kicker is a volatile position, and the difference between the No. 1 and No. 12 options is often relatively small compared with the gap at other fantasy positions.

The No. 1 kicker after three games is Evan McPherson of the Cincinnati Bengals. McPherson has made all eight of his field goal attempts this year, including a perfect five-for-five from 50-plus yards out.

It has admittedly only been three weeks, but several kickers have started out hot. Five kickers have hit on seven or more field goals without a miss—McPherson, McLaughlin, Ryan Fitzgerald of the Panthers, Will Reichard of the Vikings and Spencer Shrader of the Colts.

It has been a rockier start to the season for Jacksonville's Cam Little, who owns the NFL record for the longest field goal made. Little has missed two of his six field goal attempts this season, although one was a 70-yarder that would have set a new record.

Chris Boswell, Pittsburgh Steelers (at Cleveland Browns)

Boswell has had two big games and one clunker this season, but he's about as consistent as kickers get. Thursday night's trip to Cleveland should be another productive effort—the Browns have given up the most fantasy points in the AFC to kickers.

Harrison Butker, Kansas City Chiefs (at Las Vegas Raiders)

With the Kansas City offense rolling, Butker's off to an excellent start—he sits fifth in fantasy points among kickers. But the Raiders haven't been giving up points to the position—just four points per game.

Trey Smack, Green Bay Packers (at Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

After the Packers imploded at home last week, Smack got smacked right to the waiver wire in a lot of leagues. But he was a top-five kicker entering last week, and the Buccaneers lead the league in points surrendered to the position.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4
articles.summary: As we approach the end of the first quarter of the 2026 regular season, standout players like Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns and De'Von Achane are already out for the year, and the standings aren't quite what most expected.
articles.body:
As we approach the end of the first quarter of the 2026 regular season, standout players like Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns and De'Von Achane are already out for the year, and the standings aren't quite what most expected.

The Los Angeles Rams have fallen to 1-2, while the Las Vegas Raiders sit atop the AFC West with a flawless record.

While we're still a long way away from the November 10 trade deadline—and even further away from knowing who the true 2026 contenders are—some teams may be more aggressive in addressing needs and bolstering rosters than they were just a few weeks ago.

On Monday, the New York Giants acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Who are the top targets for this year's trade deadline buyers? Here's an updated look at our top 10 trade candidates, ranked by past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, likely availability, and relevant recent rumors.

You'll also find projected trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, along with some logical suitors.

10. Quentin Johnston, WR, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Los Angeles Chargers fell to 0-3 on Sunday, and while they may still believe they can turn their season around, they have to face the reality of their situation. Los Angeles is now staring up from the AFC West basement with no sign of catching up in the immediate future.

If the losses continue to pile up, the Chargers will have to seriously consider selling off excess pieces. Quentin Johnston has suddenly become one of them.

The fourth-year receiver topped 700 receiving yards in each of the past two seasons but has been an afterthought in Mike McDaniel's offense. He has just six catches for 64 yards through three weeks and has watched Tre' Harris take over the WR2 role opposite Ladd McConkey.

Johnston should still interest receiver-needy teams, though, as he has a high physical ceiling and another year on his rookie contract—Los Angeles did exercise his fifth-year option.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, San Francisco 49ers

9. Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 6th-Round Pick

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers also fell to 0-3 in Week 3, and they lost starting quarterback Baker Mayfield to a dislocated thumb. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that Mayfield is expected to miss at least three weeks with the injury.

Unless undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels can unleash some magic over the next few weeks, the Bucs will have a difficult time climbing out of this hole. They should strongly consider trading away running back Kenneth Gainwell, who signed a two-year, $14 million deal in the offseason.

Gainwell can be a very productive back, as evidenced by the 1,023 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns he compiled with the Pittsburgh Steelers last season. However, he hasn't been utilized in Zac Robinson's offense. He's played just 42 percent of the offensive snaps and logged a mere 16 touches so far.

With running backs like Breece Hall, Travis Etienne Jr., Jordan Mason, Isiah Pacheco, and De'Von Achane currently injured—Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL—Tampa might have an opportunity to sell relatively high here.

Potential Suitors: Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings

8. Walker Little, OT, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick and/or Veteran Defender

The Jacksonville Jaguars are sitting at 2-1 and should be buyers instead of sellers at the trade deadline. However, they're also in possession of a potentially valuable trade chip in the form of offensive tackle Walker Little.

Little has primarily played left tackle in the NFL, but he has cross-trained at other spots. The 27-year-old has never been a high-end starter, but he has appeared in 73 games with 39 starts. He can help a team seeking offensive-line depth or a capable spot starter at left tackle.

Right now, Jacksonville isn't one of those teams. It has its tackle tandem set with Anton Harrison and Cole Van Lanen. Little, meanwhile, has played just 40 total snaps on offense and special teams.

Jacksonville would likely consider flipping Little for draft capital and/or some defensive help ahead of the trade deadline. Doing so would save the Jags $11.4 million in cap space.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers

7. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick

On Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers saw starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers rebound nicely from a dreadful Week 2 performance.

At 2-1, they should still believe they can make a playoff run with the veteran at quarterback. They shouldn't be too attached to the depth they have behind him, either.

Pittsburgh carried four quarterbacks into the regular season: Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar.

Longtime NFL reporter Jason La Canfora noted at the beginning of the year that Rudolph could be available if interested teams emerged.

"The one thing stopping this is not Pittsburgh's willingness to sell, it's the number of quarterbacks potentially available across the league which could make finding a deal more difficult," La Canfora wrote for Casino.org.

The Giants' acquisition of McCarthy takes one team off the board. The Chicago Bears and Washington Commanders are probably satisfied with their quarterback situations following strong performances by Case Keenum and Marcus Mariota, respectively.

However, QB injuries will continue to mount, and not every team has a strong backup situation.

Potential Suitors: Minnesota Vikings, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 7th-Round Draft Pick

The Tennessee Titans are one of five teams sitting at 0-3, and it doesn't feel like they'll be turning around their season soon. Quarterback Cam Ward has, thus far, failed to make a Year 2 jump, while Robert Saleh has underwhelmed in his second chance as a head coach.

Defensive lineman Solomon Thomas was brought in to help Saleh revamp Tennessee's defense. He played under Saleh with the New York Jets, and he was acquired in a trade with the Dallas Cowboys.

While the Titans' defense has been sneaky good through three weeks (10th in yards and points allowed), Thomas hasn't been a big part of it. He's logged four tackles while playing just 26 percent of the defensive snaps.

Thomas is set to be a free agent in 2027, and if he isn't going to see the field often in Tennessee, the Titans should look to cash him in. He has strong rotational value, as evidenced by the 27 tackles and three tackles for loss he recorded last season.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers

5. Joey Porter Jr., CB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is back on our list, as, at least publicly, Pittsburgh's stance has changed.

During Week 2, Tracy Wolfson of CBS Sports reported that Porter had been cleared of his back injury and could return in Week 3, while the Steelers were "not actively shopping him and have not received any calls regarding him either."

Now, the Steelers are "willing to listen" to trade offers for Porter, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , and have received inquiries from teams such as the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions.

The interest is understandable, as Porter has been an above-average starter since midway through his rookie season. Pittsburgh's interest in trading him is also understandable. He will be a free agent in 2027, and the Steelers don't negotiate with players after the start of the season.

Pittsburgh is 2-1 without Porter and will risk losing him for nothing in the spring if they keep him.

The caveat here is that the Steelers will want "a strong compensation package," per Schefter. Any team dealing for him will likely also need to offer Porter a top-of-the-market contract extension. This means that only teams willing to take a big swing are likely to apply.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Detroit Lions

San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Mac Jones has fallen from our top spot for a couple of reasons. For one, the Giants, Bears, and Commanders all appear to be in better shape at quarterback than they were a week ago. Secondly, the 49ers have to be looking at all the quarterback injuries and thinking that keeping Jones is more important than ever.

Brock Purdy is playing like an MVP candidate, but he did miss eight games a season ago. Jones went 5-3 as the starter in those games and kept San Francisco on a playoff trajectory.

Obviously, the 49ers aren't planning to lose Purdy to injury again, but they've already seen injuries mount at other positions this season. Prying Jones away from San Francisco won't be cheap.

That said, the 49ers were open to moving Jones for a second-round pick in the spring, according to The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt , and they're likely to lose him in 2027 free agency. He also remains the top target for any contenders that lose their starter before November 10 or those simply looking to get a jump on next year's free-agent QB class.

Potential Suitors: Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets

The Miami Dolphins probably won't go winless in 2026, but they are 0-3 and face a brutal upcoming schedule. Furthermore, free-agent addition Malik Willis hasn't shown quite as much promise at quarterback as the team might have hoped.

Granted, Willis is playing with an underwhelming supporting cast. However, his numbers (627 yards, 1 TD, 2 INTs, 74.1 QB rating) leave plenty to be desired.

If Miami's offensive issues persist, the Dolphins could begin prioritizing 2027 and beyond—and may consider moving impending free agents such as Uche before the deadline.

Losing Achane for the season certainly won't help on that front.

Expect Miami to consider moving impending free agents like edge-rusher Josh Uche before the trade deadline. He has 11 tackles, one tackle for loss and three QB pressures this season, and he can help another team as a part-time defender.

Potential Suitors: Baltimore Ravens, New York Giants

The Cleveland Browns looked like the worst team in football during their 34-10 loss to Jacksonville in Week 1. Since then, though, they've rattled off a pair of wins and have started to see signs of life from quarterback Deshaun Watson.

Watson hasn't been great, to be fair, but he has a 104.1 passer rating and is starting to find a rhythm in Todd Monken's offense. However, he has yet to develop any real chemistry with wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.

Instead, Watson has leaned on rookie wideouts K.C. Concepcion and Denzel Boston, along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Jeudy, meanwhile, had two catches in the season opener and has logged just one target and no receptions since.

The Browns should view Jeudy as expendable, and he should retain value for receiver-needy teams. While he has largely disappointed since the start of last season, the 27-year-old was a 1,200-yard Pro Bowl receiver in 2024.

With a 2026 base salary of $1.5 million , Jeudy should fit even the tightest cap budgets.

Potential Suitors: Philadelphia Eagles, San Francisco 49ers

1. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Chargers will carry a winless record into this week's matchup with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. They face the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs after that and could realistically be 0-7 at the bye week.

It's certainly looking like it could be a lost season for Los Angeles, and the Chargers should look to cash in their trade chips while they can. Pass-rusher Khalil Mack would be a huge one ahead of the trade deadline.

While he'll turn 36 in February, Mack is still extremely effective as a rotational pass-rusher. He already has two sacks, four tackles for loss, and seven quarterback pressures this season.

Teams are always looking to add pass-rushing help, and injuries have only increased the league-wide need at the position. Myles Garrett and Nick Bosa have both been sidelined, and the New York Giants just placed Brian Burns on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL .

Potential Suitors: Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers

articles.title: Week 4 Waiver Wire Fantasy Projections for Top Pickups and Sleeper Targets
articles.summary: Winning in fantasy football takes more than just a strong draft. Managing weekly roster lineups, navigating injuries, and preparing for bye weeks are a massive part of the in-season equation.
articles.body:
Winning in fantasy football takes more than just a strong draft. Managing weekly roster lineups, navigating injuries, and preparing for bye weeks are a massive part of the in-season equation.

Byes are still a week away, but injuries have already had a major impact on the 2026 fantasy landscape. Just this past week, we saw the likes of Baker Mayfield, Justin Jefferson, Breece Hall, Travis Etienne and De'Von Achane exit with injuries.

Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL.

Fortunately, managers should be able to find a few viable fill-ins on the waiver wire this week. Here, you'll find a look at the top options and some projections for their Week 4 matchups.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Quarterbacks like Geno Smith, Kirk Cousins, and Marcus Mariota may be more readily available in some leagues. However, Carolina Panthers signal-caller Bryce Young is still only rostered in 57 percent of fantasy leagues and is a must-add this week.

Young was fantastic through the first two weeks. While he struggled against the Cleveland Browns in Week 3, he's still up to a league-high 939 passing yards with seven touchdowns and two interceptions. He also has a tremendous matchup against the Detroit Lions in Week 4.

The visiting Lions have been great offensively and far from great defensively. They rank third in scoring offense and have surrendered the most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season.

Expect Young to throw early and often as Carolina looks to keep pace on the scoreboard. Given the state of Detroit's defense, that gives him top-five scoring potential in fantasy.

Projection: 329 passing yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 12 rushing yards

With Achane out for the season, Miami Dolphins backup Ollie Gordon II has some solid long-term value and is worth picking up ahead of bye weeks. However, he's in an underwhelming offense and will face a great Minnesota Vikings defense on the road this week.

Managers looking for a Week 4 start should target New York Jets backup Braelon Allen.

Hall is considered week-to-week with a quad injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. This means we should see a lot of Allen against the Chicago Bears on Sunday.

Allen has just 72 scrimmage yards on the season, but he has logged four receptions and a touchdown. He's also rostered in only 19 percent of leagues. The Bears, meanwhile, rank a modest 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing RBs.

Projection: 67 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 18 receiving yards, 1 TD

With Alec Pierce on injured reserve, Keenan Allen has vaulted into a more prominent role with the Indianapolis Colts. He caught six passes for 63 yards and a touchdown in the Week 3 win over the Houston Texans. He should have a solid PPR floor for as long as Pierce remains sidelined.

Allen also has an enticing Week 4 matchup with the Washington Commanders on Sunday morning—yes, the Colts and Commanders play at 9:30 a.m. ET in London, so be sure to have those lineups set.

No team has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing wide receivers than Washington this season. Now, that's partially the product of facing wideouts DeVonta Smith, CeeDee Lamb, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba over the first three weeks. However, Allen still has a great amount of upside in what should be a back-and-forth offensive battle.

Allen is rostered in just 21 percent of fantasy leagues .

Projection: 7 receptions, 79 yards, 1 TD

Did we mention that the Lions' defense hasn't been very good this season? It had a really tough time corralling Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq on Sunday, and the rookie finished with seven catches, 105 yards, and a touchdown.

Sadiq will face a much stiffer challenge this week, as the Bears defense has been quite strong over the past two weeks. It has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends, though it's worth noting that Chicago hasn't faced any premier players at the position yet.

While Sadiq probably won't replicate his Week 3 production, he should be targeted early and often following his breakthrough performance in Detroit. He's rostered in only 34 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: “We were unable to bring our baby boy home”: Eli Raridon and wife Anna Raridon announce heartbreaking loss of their newborn son to anencephaly
articles.summary: Eli Raridon played college football for Notre Dame from 2022 to 2025. He married his high school sweetheart, Anna, in May 2025.
articles.body: Eli Raridon played college football for Notre Dame from 2022 to 2025. He married his high school sweetheart, Anna, in May 2025. Eli entered the NFL in 2026 as the third-round, 96th overall pick for the New England Patriots.The rookie tight end scored his first NFL touchdown on his first-ever NFL reception in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Super Bowl LX winners, the Seattle Seahawks. Three weeks into the season, he announced a heartbreaking personal loss via Instagram.“Our angel Peter James Raridon was born on September 11th. When Eli and I went in for our 20th-week anatomy scan, excited to see our sweet baby boy, our hearts were changed forever. Our little one was diagnosed with anencephaly, a fatal condition in which he would not have survive outside the womb.While we are absolutely devastated that we were unable to bring our baby boy home, I am grateful to have loved him deeply, kept him safe, and had been his home for the past 9 months before he was called back to Heaven,” Eli and Anna wrote in a collaborative Instagram post on September 29.What is anencephaly? The rare birth defect Eli Raridon and Anna’s baby boy had in the wombEli and Anna Raridon’s baby boy was diagnosed with a rare congenital abnormality called anencephaly.According to Healthline, anencephaly is a birth defect in which the brain and bones of the skull don’t form completely while the baby is in the womb. As a result, the baby’s brain, particularly the cerebral cortex, develops minimally. The cerebral cortex controls thinking, movement, and senses like touch, vision, and hearing.According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, anencephaly is a serious birth defect where a baby is born without parts of the brain and skull at birth.As of January 2026, the incurable condition affects 1 in every 4,762 babies born with anencephaly in the United States.Risk factors include low folate levels in pregnancy, pre-existing health conditions like uncontrolled diabetes, certain medications such as anti-seizure medicines, and overheating [getting in a hot tub] or fever.The condition can be diagnosed during pregnancy using tests to check for birth defects and other conditions. Being pregnant with an anencephaly baby can result in an abnormal result on blood or serum tests. Anencephaly can also be seen on an ultrasound exam.The expected outcome is that there is no cure or standard treatment for anencephaly. Pregnancy loss is high. Almost all babies born with anencephaly will die shortly after birth.Eli and Anna Raridon may never understand the whyThe 22-year-old rookie tight end Eli Raridon and his wife, Anna, further wrote in the Instagram post, “We may never understand the why behind this journey, but one thing we know with certainty is that God promises to care for His children.I believe our little boy was lovingly knitted together in the womb by God, knowing how deeply he would be loved by our families, our friends, Eli, and me.Though his time with us was brief, his life still precious, his purpose still meaningful, and he will forever be a part of our story. I have loved you every second of your life & will miss you every second of mine. What a sweet sweet reunion ours will be.”Eli Raridon and Anna had announced their first pregnancy via Instagram in April 2026.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Panthers' Xavier Legette grateful for teammates, including QB Bryce Young, experiencing his country lifestyle
articles.summary: Xavier Legette brought Carolina Panthers teammates including Bryce Young to his small South Carolina hometown for a trail ride and raccoon dinner.
articles.body: Carolina Panthers wide receiver Xavier Legette loves the game of football, but back home in Mullins, South Carolina, a true country lifestyle is how he, his family and friends love to spend their time. Whether it’s taking care of his horses, which NFL fans have come quite familiar with since the Panthers took him in the first round in 2024 out of South Carolina, fishing, or riding around town on what he calls a "trail ride," Legette’s southern roots are shown in full force whenever he’s back home. Before the 2026 season, Legette was able to show some of his Panthers teammates what it’s like in his small South Carolina town that has less than 4,000 residents, including his quarterback, Bryce Young. Sports Illustrated was along for the ride, as Legette showcased a day in his life with the entire town alongside him for the trail ride. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE It was an experience that had Legette quite grateful, not just for himself and allowing his teammates to experience the special side of his life off the field, but for the people in Mullins. "To tell you the truth, man, that part of it was great -- for them to be able to come and do those things. But I think the best thing really in my eyes about the whole situation was them boys being able to come in my community," he told OutKick in a recent interview, while highlighting his partnership with Bojangles. "People in my community being able to see other people other than me, you know what I’m saying? Because they always see me." PANTHERS' BRYCE YOUNG, XAVIER LEGETTE SPEND OFFSEASON WEEKEND RIDING HORSES AND RIPPING ATVS Legette, with his southern accent and unique hobbies, has become a fan-favorite in the Panthers community, as well as the NFL in general. Viral moments, from his first news conference after being drafted to telling folks he didn’t mind trying asparagus for the first time, made him someone football fans couldn’t get enough of. Legette is nothing but positive and genuine, two of the many characteristics he had growing up surrounded by the people he loved most in his small town. Now that he’s at this stage of professional life, all he wishes to do is give back and grow the place he still, and will always, call home. Having Panthers teammates there to see that meant the world to him. "I grew up there and I’m one of the first ones to be able to be in this position that I am being from Marion County." he added. "So just being able for them to see other faces, they was excited. "Everyone know everybody, but my family, it stands out to me, you know what I’m saying? They’re the ones that helped me able to [do this]. They shaped me into being who I am today. I got my love for them. It’s out of this world and being able to just go through the growing pains with them, ups and downs, and then it’s nothing but smiles on their face. That’s what I love to see." Oh, and one of those viral moments mentioned before includes his admittance to eating raccoon, squirrel and other animals that he and his family find on hunts. When his teammates were in town, they had to try the local cuisine. "Oh yeah, we had the raccoon out there. A couple of them tried it," Legette said, noting that Young left early before it was ready. Fellow receiver David Moore was among those who tried the raccoon. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! COUNTRY MEETS SPOOKY Legette’s southern lifestyle is one that came to life for a one-of-a-kind content series by Pepsi and Bojangles, and it stars one of his prized horses, affectionately known as Dime Piece, as Halloween and football come together. Legette had a smile ear-to-ear as he discussed the Bojangles Bite Box which, starting Oct. 1, will come with limited-edition haunted house packaging. "I think it’s a great collab. It’s one of the biggest ones I’ve ever did, and man, I hope we can come up with something else for the future. "They understand my love for the horses and they wanted to bring that to life with this commercial. It’s great." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD While Legette will be heading to Bojangles whenever he can to get his Bite Box, he’s also excited for another Halloween, where he might just have to be his favorite superhero yet again. "All I wanted to be was Spider-Man every year," he said, laughing.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current face billion-dollar twist as Chris and Angie Long eye 6,500-seat expansion
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current are preparing to make their already successful home even bigger.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current are preparing to make their already successful home even bigger. CPKC Stadium, the first venue built specifically for a professional women’s sports team, has quickly become one of the NWSL’s most sought-after destinations. With thousands of fans waiting for tickets, the club is now considering a major expansion that could add 6,500 seats. Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are part of the Current’s ownership group, while Chris and Angie Long privately financed the stadium’s construction.KC Current look to expand CPKC StadiumWhen Chris and Angie Long began planning a dedicated home for the Kansas City Current, there was no obvious blueprint to follow. NWSL teams had traditionally shared venues with men’s clubs, leaving the owners to rethink what a women’s soccer stadium could look like.They opted for a smaller setting with 11,500 seats, taking inspiration from compact venues known for intense atmospheres. The idea was simple: create a ground where supporters felt close to the action and demand for tickets remained strong.That strategy quickly paid off.CPKC Stadium opened in March 2024 as Kansas City’s enthusiasm for women’s soccer was growing. The Current then made league history by selling out every home match during their opening season at the venue.The club’s ticket demand has remained strong. Its season-ticket base now stands at about 8,000, while more than 5,000 people are reportedly waiting for an opportunity to secure tickets. Only a limited number of seats are available for individual matches.The stadium’s premium spaces have also attracted strong demand. All 12 luxury suites, which require long-term commitments, sold out within roughly two weeks.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes back Kansas City CurrentThe success has created a problem many sports owners would welcome, but it is still a problem. A stadium designed to feel intimate is struggling to accommodate everyone who wants to attend.Chris Long acknowledged the tension between maintaining scarcity and allowing more supporters through the gates.“Sometimes scarcity is a really, really good thing, but sometimes it puts people off, too,” says Chris Long, who in addition to owning the Current serves as chairman and CEO of Palmer Square Capital Management, the investment firm he cofounded with his wife that has more than $36 billion in assets under management and is based just across the Kansas border in Mission Woods. “We want to get more people in the tent.”The proposed addition of 6,500 seats would significantly increase capacity while allowing the Current to preserve the identity that helped make CPKC Stadium successful.For the ownership group, including Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the expansion could also mark another stage in the rapid growth of the Kansas City Current and the wider business of women’s professional soccer.The challenge will be balancing greater access with the close, energetic atmosphere that made the stadium such a draw in the first place.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Amid a disastrous start for the Tennessee Titans offense, Cam Ward is not in immediate danger of losing his job as their starting quarterback.
articles.body:
Amid a disastrous start for the Tennessee Titans offense, Cam Ward is not in immediate danger of losing his job as their starting quarterback.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the feeling right now is the Titans want to give Ward more time to figure things out as he learns new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's system.

"Accuracy and decision-making are issues, but the Titans hope he will build off the late-game growing pains. He also isn't turning the ball over at a high clip (one interception through three games) and the team values his makeup and work ethic," Fowler wrote.

In the same report for ESPN, Dan Graziano noted there is a "sense" that things are "out of whack" with the Titans:

"I'm talking about the overall environment around the team, not just Ward. There's an obvious disconnect between Ward and the coaching staff, or at least the scheme, and the time to address and adjust those things was the spring and summer. How do the Titans fix lingering structural issues with their offense and with Ward's development during the season? There's still widespread belief that Ward has the character and the ability to weather early-career struggles and come out stronger for it. But there's also a sense around the league that it should look better than it does right now, and there's curiosity about what's preventing the improvement from happening."

The Titans are 3-17 in Ward's 20 starts since the beginning of the 2025 season. Their offense finished 30th in points per game during his rookie year and ranks 30th in points per game through three weeks in 2026.

Ward's 33.2 QBR as a rookie ranked last out of 28 qualified quarterbacks. His 47.2 QBR so far this season is an improvement, but it's still only good enough for 23rd out of 30 quarterbacks.

Tennessee has scored 10 or fewer points in three of its last four games dating back to Week 18 last season. Ward has yet to throw for 200 yards in a game this season. His last game with multiple touchdown passes was against the New Orleans Saints in Week 17 last year.

Even with the lack of receiving talent on the Titans roster, Ward has had instances of not seeing open players or missing them when he does find them. There was a play in the third quarter against the Giants when Carnell Tate was wide open in the end zone and Ward sailed a pass over his head.

Ward's primary attribute to this point has been not throwing interceptions. He has eight interceptions in 628 career attempts, but it's clear from his performance that the rest of his game isn't working right now.

The struggles for Ward and the offense are also overshadowing the job first-year head coach Robert Saleh has done to elevate the defense. They have been far from perfect on that side of the ball, particularly trying to stop the run, but they rank 10th in points allowed and seventh in pass yards allowed.

Tennessee's next game is against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. The Titans' bye isn't until Week 9, so presumably things will have to improve for Ward before then if there is already speculation about a potential change.

Mitchell Trubisky is the No. 2 quarterback on Tennessee's depth chart. He hasn't started a game since Week 15 of the 2023 season for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

articles.title: 2026 NFL Season: Roger Goodell rooting for Lamar Jackson, Tom Brady backing Josh Allen, and Jeff Bezos cheering on Dak Prescott
articles.summary: Roger Goodell recently praised Lamar Jackson’s impact.
articles.body: Roger Goodell recently praised Lamar Jackson’s impact. When a reporter asked, “What has Lamar meant to the league?” the NFL commissioner said,“Well, you're not an MVP multiple times, you know, because you're not a superstar. But, you know, he just brings an excitement to the game that's just really explosive. And it's fun for everyone to be able to see it.”Goodell continued, “Nobody feels like they're out of a game when you have Lamar on your side, right? And so I just think that kind of talent - he's changed the game. He's actually changed the way that position is played. And you can't say that about a lot of guys.”It feels like the NFL commissioner is rooting for that one NFL player without a Super Bowl. For that one elite quarterback who has repeatedly come up short in his pursuit of a championship. For that one player whose explosive style has changed the way the quarterback position is viewed.What does it say about the unwavering faith? It says Lamar Jackson remains an undefeated warrior. Like Joe Burrow, the 29-year-old signal-caller who continues to pick up his broken pieces after every setback and return the next season with renewed willpower, strength, and determination.Tom Brady supports Josh AllenTom Brady, who could never choose between Patriots and Buccaneers, has finally shown his support for Josh Allen. He calls him one of the NFL’s most prominent quarterbacks.“I don’t think there’s anyone playing better than him in the NFL. he just does an awesome job from the pocket. I think he’s doing a great job when his first reads open and Joe Brady calls a good play drops back his first guy’s open,” Brady said.“Just the rare talent that can stand in there beat you from the pockey and then when you actually play pretty good coverage, he breaks the pocket and then still just does a lot of damage to these defenses. So he is neatly impossible to stop.”The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB knows what it takes to handle the immense pressure that comes with being the sole face of a franchise.Tom Brady spent 23 NFL seasons dealing with constant championship expectations and has often spoken highly of QBs who possess the physical ability and leadership required to compete at the highest level on the gridiron.Josh Allen has emerged as one of the NFL’s most popular stars during his time with the Buffalo Bills.His unique combination of arm strength, mobility, and ability to make plays under immense pressure has made him one of the league’s biggest quarterback names to-date.Coming from NFL legend Tom Brady, whose career included seven Super Bowl victories, any praise for Josh Allen carries added level of significance. Brady has experienced literally every stage of an NFL quarterback’s career, from early struggles to postseason heartbreak, and unique championship success.For Allen, the challenge remains transforming his unique individual brilliance and the Buffalo Bills’ expected regular-season success into another deep postseason run [but this time going all the way!]And with Brady backing him, the rare spotlight on Allen remains as radiant as ever heading into the 2026 NFL season. Three wins in the bag, already.Jeff Bezos cheers Dak PrescottAs for Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos? The megabusiness tycoon indirectly supports the Dallas Cowboys’ quarterback Dak Prescott.The Washington Post owner attended the Cowboys vs. Commanders game on September 21. Jeff Bezos made it crystal clear that he was rooting for the Dallas Cowboys.“I have a couple thoughts. One, I really want the Cowboys to win today,” Jeff Bezos said via Chris Amaya of the Dallas Morning News in September 2026.“Second is the field energy here. It’s such great energy here. There’s something special about this [Dallas Cowboys] stadium…About this team, and of course, something special about [Cowboys owner] Jerry [Jones]. It’s great to be his guest.”Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was more than happy to have the Amazon founder’s physical presence supporting his team.“What he is, is a part of what we all are proud of, and that’s being a part of America,” Jones said. “It’s quite a privilege. Like I said, I pulled out all the stops to try and give us some energy to win this game today.”The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Washington Commanders in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season, 37-20, at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026. Once again, there's concern about Williams being in a timeshare with Blake Corum . And again, it doesn't appear to be an issue. For the second straight week, Williams' workload increased. This time it was 15 carries for 88 yards and six catches for another 70 yards.

Barkley was back on the field and has returned to full health after missing the majority of Week 2's game. He's yet to rush for a touchdown this season, but it's hard to argue with a performance nearly identical to Week 1: 15 carries for 78 yards.

Jeanty has a workload each week, but he's yet to gain traction. In Week 3, he managed 56 yards on 19 carries (2.9 yards per carry). Jeanty has yet to rush for a touchdown this season, but he also has 13 catches for 97 yards.

It doesn't matter what country Henry is playing in, you know exactly what he's going to do. In this case, Henry rushed for two touchdowns, six on the season, while gaining 89 yards on 24 carries. This just never gets old.

It's unclear how this will play out by the end of the season, but for now, it's working great for Cook. For the second straight week, he averaged 6.4 yards per carry and finished with 24 carries for 154 yards and a touchdown. With that level of production, who cares that he didn't catch a pass?

Aug 6, 2026; Santa Clara, CA, USA; San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey (23) during training camp at SAP Performance Facility. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

5. Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The 49ers are taking things slow with McCaffrey this season, and there are no issues with that. In Week 3, it meant 15 carries for 75 yards and a touchdown. That came with four catches for 41 yards. It's a performance we would take every time.

Walker continues to play a large role in Kansas City's offense, and we are getting quality to match the quantity. He picked up a touchdown both on the ground and through the air while touching the ball 20 times. Perhaps things get a little hard against the Raiders this week, but there's no need for concern.

After two straight weeks of two touchdowns each, Taylor failed to crack the end zone in Week 3. He found it difficult, rightfully so, to find room to run against the Houston Texans and finished with 20 carries for 68 yards.

We expected the offense to be better with Michael Penix under center, but did we expect 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns? Atlanta will continue to rely heavily on Robinson, and he's very much up to the task.

The nerve of Gibbs falling short of the century mark. All he did was carry the ball 20 times for 99 yards and two touchdowns. We should add, though, that Gibbs also caught seven passes for 65 yards and another touchdown. Yes, he's pretty good.

articles.title: The Betting Trends Shaking Up The NFL After Three Weeks
articles.summary: NFL Week 3 betting trends: who is hot, who is down and who is making moves that are shaping the market as the season heads into Week 4.
articles.body:
Who saw this coming? Week three in the NFL was supposed to be the week that we could look at and say, "Ok, I know who is good and who isn't." That can't be further from the truth. Chaos rules and we should have seen it coming. I mean last Thursday night practically screamed at us. It's overreaction time in the NFL witha betting slant and boy do I have an abundance of them.

Las Vegas is undefeated. Cleveland is tied for first in their division. Houston and New England are in disarray. Seattle lost to Washington (without Jayden Daniels ). What is going on? Well, a few things as I see it.

Let's give credit to new coaches in certain places. Cleveland, Las Vegas and Arizona have completely changed their culture (I know that's a tired cliche, but it works). Las Vegas came back from a 11-point second half deficit to win on the road in New Orleans . Cleveland kept their composure and won late against Carolina. Arizona played Sam Francisco tough before falling short. John Harbaugh has something cooking in New York….maybe. Call it parity, call it the cyclical nature of the NFL. It's just their turn.

The schedule also is in play. Las Vegas has had a fairly easy schedule thus far. Sunday was a step up and they passed that test. Their defensive front is legit. They rattled a usually unflappable Tyler Shough and seized control of a game they were behind by double digits in. That's the mark of a good team. Cleveland has played two teams from the NFC South. That's enough to pad anyone's record. The South is absolutely dreadful.

You can chalk up Seattle losing to the odds. No one goes undefeated and almost everyone loses one they're supposed to win. Ditto Cincinnati , although I see problems with their defense (I thought they were markedly improved). Houston and New England are the big questions. The Texans have been competitive but they're not benefitting from a tough schedule at the beginning. New England looks just dreadful. Maybe the Vrabel drama affected everyone? Can't say for sure but this team in no way resembles the AFC Championship squad from a year ago.

Updated playoff odds: Las Vegas +165 Cleveland +500 New York Giants +350 New England -110 (really???)

Two games I saw today have me scratching my head. The Las Vegas Raiders turned up the defense and took one away from New Orleans. Or should I say, Kellen Moore couldn't see what was in front of him and called a terrible game. The Saints offense was predictable and unimaginative. Tyler Shough was a sitting duck in the pocket. He's mobile and can make off schedule throws when it all breaks down. That's when he's at his best. Moore gave him no option. He's supposed to be the next great offensive mind. Sunday he wasn't.

The Los Angeles/San Diego Chargers are in the same boat. Jim Harbaugh has turned Justin Herbert into a backup. The Chargers had the ball with the lead in the fourth quarter and Harbaugh put Herbert in positions to turn the ball over, which he did. In the red zone of all places too. These head coaches outsmart themselves sometimes. Let the players do what they do best. It's not always a chess game. Harbaugh and Moore are playing checkers. And they suck at it.

Updated playoff odds: New Orleans +105 Los Angeles Chargers +500

We know who the Super Bowl contenders are

It's a short list. Buffalo and Kansas City have already separated themselves in the AFC. Baltimore , Jacksonville, Cincinnati will be in the mix. In the NFC, it's Seattle and San Francisco . With the possible exception of Philadelphia nobody else looks like a serious contender. Keep an eye on Minnesota though. They won again despite losing Justin Jefferson early. Of course, they were playing Tampa Bay. Goodness the South is awful.

Super Bowl odds: Buffalo +650 Sam Francisco +900 Seattle +1100 Kansas City +1100

My final four as of today. It can and will change because in today's NFL the only thing for sure is nothing's for sure.

articles.title: How much more aggressive have the NFL and Bills gotten in end-of-half situations?
articles.summary: How much more aggressive has the NFL gotten at the end of the first half?
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have scored two touchdowns in the final two minutes through three games to begin their 2026 season, and of course, for the vast majority of the Josh Allen era, the team has embraced aggression in the final few minutes before halftime.

And in Week 3, we saw the Ravens make a game-winning field goal against the Cowboys in Rio De Janeiro on a drive that began with 0:07 remaining in the contest. That highly entertaining game also featured a Brandon Aubrey field goal with 0:18 left in the first half.

In watching the NFL for over 30 years now, I've noticed what has felt like a drastic change in league-wide philosophy when it's come to the end of the first half scenarios for offenses. It's seemingly had a major impact on overall coring in the NFL. Those last two minutes of the second quarter normally take forever, don't they?

I've wanted to study this paradigm shift for a while now to see if what I'd been feeling observationally was actually true and to what extent the perceived shift has taken place. I used 25 years of nflverse play-by-play data to finally do so.

Here's the foundational table in this investigation, which shows the amount of combined points scored in the final two minutes of games compared to overall scoring changes:

The 4.00 points to 4.77 points finding represents a 19.3% increase in scoring during the final two minutes over the span of the last 25 years. That's nearly triple the percentage increase in overall scoring during that time frame. The jump from 41.94 to 45.02 is only a 7.3% increase.

And this didn't happen purely by chance. To demonstrate how much more aggressive the NFL has gotten over the past quarter century, check the gradual albeit steady growth in dropback rate in these situations in the 25-year sample:

Yes, there was a bit of a dip from the 2016 – 2020 segment compared to the most recent 2021 – 2025 segment, yet a clear increase from the 74.2% at the beginning segment in this study. Only an increase of 6% points? Ehh, not much, right?

Let's dig a little deeper and narrow the scope regarding no-huddle rate, which should serve as a clear indication of play-caller aggression in these late-half scenarios.

When the clock was between 0:31 and 1:00 remaining in the half, the no-huddle rate erupted from 2.9% in the 2001 – 2005 segment to 22.6% in 2021 – 2025.

When zooming out, the same theme is present. Here's NFL-wide dropback rate by time remaining in the first half:

Another indicator of a widespread philosophical change late in the first half. Dropback rate was up nearly 10 percentage points in the final minute of the first half across the board when comparing 2021 – 2025 to 2001 – 2025.

And it the paradigm shift has generated so much more scoring in the time crunch before halftime. This is where the percentages have moved outrageously. Here are percentage of drives that ended in a score of any kind (field goal or touchdown), sorted by time remaining at time of first snap of the possession:

How about this more narrowly focused scenario:

First scrimmage snap with 45–120 seconds remaining

*there were over 490 total possessions in every five-year segment

At this point, these percentage increases shouldn't be surprising. More signs of aggression — first-play dropback rate rose from 59.6% in the first segment to 70.4% in the most recent segment, and it resulted in much more scoring — 25.2% of drives ended in a score in 2001 – 2025 vs. 37.2% ending in a score in 2021 – 2025.

I also wanted to find the sweet spot for NFL teams, when they have started to feel the most comfortable trying to put points on the board near the end of the half compared to how it used to be. And I wanted to sort by field position, score margin, and timeouts remaining because those feel like contributing factors to coach's end-of-half decisions, right?

Here's the data with 45–60 seconds remaining, with the drive starting in a team's own territory, game within one score, and the offense with at least one timeout.

In 2001 – 2025, teams were dropping back to pass on the first play in those scenarios almost exactly one out of every two times, and most recently, it's happening more than three out of every four times. Enormous leap.

If the scenario is tweaked to the team possessing the ball actually having a lead of 1-8 points, the first-play dropback rate went from 52.1% in 2001 – 2005 to 65.5% in 2021 – 2025 , and, more strikingly, percentage of drives ending with a score more than doubled from 22.1% in the earliest time frame to 44.8% from 2021 – 2025.

That's truly game-changing. Across the entire league.

Have these trends continued early in the 2026 NFL season? And how have the Bills attacked the end of the first half?

During the 2021 – 2025 segment, mostly due to the presence of Josh Allen, the Bills unsurprisingly stayed ahead of the NFL averages. In the final two minutes, Buffalo's dropback rate was 82.1% vs. 80.0% league-wide. And its no-huddle rate was 16.5% vs. 15.7% league-wide.

Fascinatingly, the Bills averaged a whopping 3.02 points per game in the final two minutes between 2021 – 2025, while their opponents only averaged 1.57 points in that scenario during that time segment.

The 2026 sample is significantly smaller than the rest of the study, but the league has stayed mostly the same in all the scenarios listed above. Offenses have dropped back to pass in the final two minutes on 79.7% of their plays (vs. 80.0% from 2021 – 2025). When there's between 31 – 60 seconds left, the dropback rate has been 88.6% thus far in 2026. That's up from 85.5% in 2021 – 2025.

League-wide scoring is slightly down (4.54) compared to the 2021 – 2025 segment (4.77) in the final minute of the half, but I expect that to change as the season progresses.

As for the Bills this season, they have 16 qualifying plays in the final two minutes of the half entering Week 4. Their overall dropback rate in those scenarios is 81.3%, and they have a no-huddle rate of 18.8%. The NFL's no-huddle rate through Week 3 was only 13.4%. They've scored an average of 4.67 points in the final two minutes — they have two touchdowns in the final two minutes of the first half in three games.

If you've made it this far, you are officially as nerdy as me when it comes to the NFL.

I have another, to me, equally as captivating part to this study that I'll release in the next few weeks.

But, yes, the NFL has gotten drastically more aggressive — and better at scoring — late in the first half. Compared to 25 years ago, those minutes have become entirely different, which has had a major impact on the entire game itself.

articles.title: New Anthony Richardson Trade Rumors Update Colts QB's Availability After J.J. McCarthy to Giants
articles.summary: In the aftermath of the J.J. McCarthy trade to the New York Giants, the quarterback market is now open with Anthony Richardson being another intriguing former first-rounder a team might look to take a flyer on.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of the J.J. McCarthy trade to the New York Giants, the quarterback market is now open with Anthony Richardson being another intriguing former first-rounder a team might look to take a flyer on.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler , there is no indication right now that the Indianapolis Colts are looking to trade Richardson.

Graziano noted the Colts might be "willing to take less to move on" from Richardson later in the season since he is in the final year of his rookie contract and they try to get anything they can in return.

According to Fowler, the Giants never called Indianapolis to inquire about Richardson's status before they made the deal with the Minnesota Vikings for McCarthy.

"Richardson would welcome the chance to learn behind the scenes in the McVay or Shanahan trees, but that doesn't feel feasible, at least this season," Fowler wrote.

Colts general manager Chris Ballard told reporters at the start of training camp that Richardson requested a trade, but the team was "not going to give him away."

Richardson, despite by his own admission not having a great camp, did win the Colts' backup job. His talent and ability remain more theoretical than anything else simply because he hasn't played much, especially of late.

The 24-year-old's last start was in Week 16 of the 2024 season. His last appearance was in Week 5 last season when he played seven snaps in garbage time of the Colts' 40-6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Indianapolis declined Richardson's fifth-year option in April, making him eligible for free agency at the end of this season. It wouldn't be a surprise if a quarterback-needy team wanted to get him in the building at some point this year to see what their coaching staff can do to help develop him, then decide on whether or not to re-sign him in the offseason.

articles.title: Vikings Insiders Dish on 'Brutal' J.J. McCarthy Era, 'Eye-Rolls' About 'Nine' Nickname
articles.summary: It sounds like the Minnesota Vikings won't be looking back fondly at the J.J. McCarthy era after this week's trade with the New York Giants.
articles.body:
It sounds like the Minnesota Vikings won't be looking back fondly at the J.J. McCarthy era after this week's trade with the New York Giants.

The Athletic's Alec Lewis spoke to a team staffer who revealed that the Vikings had lost faith in McCarthy since his disappointing 2025 season.

"I knew this was going to be up and down when we made that choice this spring (to move forward with McCarthy as the starter), but it has just been brutal," the staffer said.

The Vikings moved up in the 2024 NFL draft to select McCarthy 10th overall. His shortcomings were quickly on display, as Lewis reported that "in the immediate aftermath of the draft, several team sources acknowledged that McCarthy had work to do. He would have to eliminate his overstriding on throws and develop better touch."

After missing his entire rookie year due to knee surgery, McCarthy was handed the reins as Minnesota's starting quarterback entering the 2025 campaign. However, he struggled to stay healthy and appeared in just 10 games due to multiple injuries, finishing with 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. The Vikings brought in veteran signal-caller Kyler Murray this offseason, and McCarthy was demoted to QB3 behind him and veteran backup Carson Wentz.

Lewis also explained that McCarthy's immaturity affected his tenure in Minnesota. His comments regarding his "Nine" alter ego reportedly "earned several internal eye-rolls," and he "similarly baffled members of the organization when he told reporters that he bucked his coaches' advice by dancing the 'Griddy' before he reached the end zone against the Cowboys in Week 15."

"These bouts of youth and defiance, evident both in front of the cameras and away from them inside the TCO Performance Center, were troubling for Vikings executives and coaches," Lewis added.

Now, McCarthy will have to win over a new franchise as he makes a fresh start with the Giants, who acquired him after second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. He will serve as the backup to veteran signal-caller Jameis Winston, so he should use the rest of the 2026 season to learn and develop as he tries to revive his reputation.
