articles.title: Sean McVay Reportedly Eyed by Amazon for 'TNF' Role amid Kirk Herbstreit Contract Extension
articles.summary: Four years after Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay considered stepping away from the sidelines to become a broadcaster, Amazon is still keeping the door open for him to join the Thursday Night Football team in the future.
articles.body:
Four years after Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay considered stepping away from the sidelines to become a broadcaster, Amazon is still keeping the door open for him to join the Thursday Night Football team in the future.

Per The Athletic's Andrew Marchand , Kirk Herbstreit has agreed to a contract extension with Prime Video to remain part of the Thursday Night Football broadcast crew.

However, Marchand noted the agreement with Herbstreit offers Amazon some "flexibility" to get out of the deal "if one of its top targets, like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, becomes available" in the future.

Coming off the Rams' Super Bowl 56 victory in February 2021, reports started coming out that McVay could be offered a deal worth more than $15 million annually if he ever wanted to move into broadcasting.

Marchand reported Amazon was prepared to give McVay a deal worth up to $100 million over five years.

After a difficult 2022 season in which injuries to several key players led to the Rams finished with a 5-12 record, McVay went through a period when it was unclear if he would continue coaching.

In February 2023, The Athletic's Jourdan Rodrigue reported throughout the 2022 season McVay "spiraled under a wave of self-destruction, fatigue, grief and frustration."

McVay admitted earlier this year on the Bussin with the Boys podcast (h/t Ryan Anderson of the California Post ) that he felt like "a fraud" during the 2022 campaign.

"The reality is, I would have been quitting because I couldn't handle the losing. It was almost like a scarlet letter," McVay added.

The Rams announced in January 2023 that McVay informed the club he was returning as head coach.

If McVay were to walk away from coaching to go into broadcasting, his asking price will almost certainly be significantly higher than what Amazon was reportedly offering in 2022.

Tom Brady is currently the highest-paid NFL broadcaster with a $37.5 million annual salary from Fox.

Troy Aikman is currently making $18 million per season from ESPN as the color commentator for Monday Night Football. He is in the final year of his current deal with talks between the two sides expected to wait until after the Super Bowl.

Exact details of coaching contracts are hard to come by, but as of September 2025, McVay was believed to be making $15 million annually from the Rams.

Since the first — and to date, only — losing season of his coaching career in 2022, McVay has led the Rams to the playoffs in each of the last three seasons. They lost in the NFC Championship Game to the Seattle Seahawks in January.

McVay owns a 93-59 overall record with seven playoff appearances, two trips to the Super Bowl and one victory in 10 seasons as Rams head coach.

articles.title: New Jayden Daniels Injury Update as Commanders QB Resumes Throwing at Practice
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has taken a "good step" in recovery from his elbow injury ahead of a Week 4 matchup in London, head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Wednesday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has taken a "good step" in recovery from his elbow injury ahead of a Week 4 matchup in London, head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Wednesday.

Quinn said the Commanders had not yet ruled out Daniels for Sunday's game ahead of his limited participation in Wednesday's "jog-through" practice.

"As we're working through the week, he'll get more reps... As we get into Thursday and Friday, we'll see what that load looks like," Quinn said. "And then by Friday we'll have a definite determination of where we're at."

Quinn continued, "We're not going to put him out there before he's ready, so that's why it's important for us to trust the process as we're going. But him being back on the field is like, man, that's a good step for us."

ESPN's John Keim shared videos of Daniels throwing with a brace on his left arm.

The Commanders are preparing for a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff this Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts in London.

Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow on an awkward fall during the Commanders' Week 2 loss at the Dallas Cowboys.

The Commanders said shortly afterward Daniels was not considering surgery on the elbow, which also sidelined him for stretches last season.

The team decided not to place him on IR, indicating a possible return within four weeks, and kept the possibility of a start against the Colts open by bringing Daniels with the team to the United Kingdom.

After suffering a left elbow dislocation in Week 9 of the 2025 season, Daniels briefly returned in Week 14 wearing a brace before re-injuring the elbow and leaving the game early.

Multiple reporters noted Daniels is expected to once more wear a left arm brace upon his return from his latest elbow dislocation.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Daniels' brace will be "bulkier" than the one he briefly wore last season but "should not limit what he has to do on the field."

The Commanders (1-2) are looking to get back to .500 with a win over the Colts (1-2), which have ranked 30th in passing yards allowed through three games.

Should Daniels remain sidelined Sunday, Marcus Mariota would be tabbed to make a second straight start for the Commanders.

Mariota started last Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, where he went 10-for-31 with 183 passing yards and three touchdowns in a win over the defending Super Bowl champions.

If not the past, then his present and future.Justin Herbert faces brutal Gridiron Heights satire over Chargers’ 2026 strugglesThe latest Gridiron Heights episode from Bleacher Report turns the ongoing NFL debate surrounding Justin Herbert into a courtroom comedy.The episode asks whether the Los Angeles Chargers quarterback is as good as advertised.The episode casts Herbert as a defendant, poking fun at the immense scrutiny he’s faced throughout his NFL career.The satire arrives at a crucial point in Herbert’s career. articles.title: Andrew Luck still has no regrets about early NFL retirement: 'I’m right where I’m supposed to be'
articles.summary: Andrew Luck's retirement in 2019 remains a fascinating topic for football fans.
articles.body:
Andrew Luck has always seemed more content about his early NFL retirement than the rest of us.

It seems like Luck retired just a bit ago, but it has been a while. More time has passed since Luck's retirement in 2019 (2,594 days) than the length of his NFL career (2,540 days from his debut to retirement). And yet, Luck still remains a curious figure because of the abruptness and surprise of his retirement, which he said was due to an unrelenting cycle of injuries and rehab. He's just 37 years old. Kirk Cousins , who has helped the Las Vegas Raiders to a 3-0 start and was in the 2012 NFL Draft like Luck, is 38.

For a few years after the retirement it was a pastime of fans to project a Luck comeback every time a quarterback got hurt, but that comeback never happened. Luck is happy with his job as the general manager of Stanford's football program. And he said this week he has no regrets.

"Nope," Luck said during an interview with Yahoo Sports Daily . "Not to say it wasn't a hard [decision], it was the hardest decision of my life probably up until that point, and maybe since as well, but no. It was exactly what needed to happen for me. Again, not an easy one, but the right one."

Had Luck never retired, he could still be playing and presumably doing so at a high level. Matthew Stafford , who won his first MVP last season, is a year older than Luck. But Luck will let everyone else worry about what might have happened, because he doesn't do so himself.

Andrew Luck watched Philip Rivers from afar

Plenty of quarterbacks get the itch to return. Philip Rivers was coaching high school football when he came out of retirement to play for the Indianapolis Colts late last season. Drew Brees said he thought about coming out of retirement for the Denver Broncos when they lost Bo Nix to injury before the AFC championship game last season, and texted Denver assistants Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi, his offensive coordinator and quarterback coach when he was with the Saints.

Rivers is seven years older than Luck, and didn't have the history with the Colts that Luck did. But Luck says the Colts didn't call him asking about a return.

"I have an amazing relationship with Chris Ballard, the GM of the Colts, amazing," Luck told Yahoo Sports Daily. "I consider him a mentor of mine, we have been through some 'ish' together and come out the other side and have a stronger relationship, so no. We are on the same page there."

Luck was interested in watching though. He said he was at a 49ers game with recently hired Stanford head coach Tavita Pritchard during Rivers' first game back since 2020, and was watching the Colts play the Seahawks on his iPhone.

"Like 99.9% of America, I was fascinated by Philip coming back and playing, and playing at a high level, and doing it as a grandfather," Luck said.

He just didn't have the desire to do it himself.

If Luck had continued to play, and was paid at or near the top of the quarterback pay scale every season since his retirement, he would have made more than $400 million more in career earnings from the NFL and counting.

Most people couldn't fathom stepping away from the fame and fortune of being an NFL quarterback just before you turn 30 years old, with perhaps a decade left to play. Then there's Luck, who reacted to a question about stepping away from the NFL by saying he was "stoked" about an espresso he just had.

"No regrets, and not to say I did things perfectly by any stretch of the imagination," Luck told Yahoo Sports Daily. "I learned a bunch from both the successful moments and the low moments of playing as a professional quarterback and for the Colts. But I think, life keeps moving forward. Thankful for the opportunites I had and I also feel full of purpose and passion as the general manager of Stanford football . I love this school, I love this program, there's a real mission we're on. I love working with these young men. I love our coaching staff.

"I'm right where I'm supposed to be. I have an amazing wife and two amazing daughters. Life keeps throwing wonderful pleasant gifts along the way."

After some years completely out of the spotlight, Luck came back to football with Stanford. He said he still believes in the character development that comes along with the sport. But he understands the darker side of football. When Joe Burrow wondered aloud last season, after multiple injuries, why he'd keep playing football if it wasn't fun anymore, everyone made the comparison to Luck stepping away right in his prime. Luck knows the toll the game can take.

"I think the majority of professional athletes go through questions like this at various points in their career," Luck said, when asked about Burrow. "That's part of being a professional athlete. Especially in a trying, violent — football is not a contact sport, it's a collision sport, and it can be trying."

And Luck had enough of that life as a player. He hasn't looked back.

articles.title: New Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors on Cowboys Links, Steelers CB's Valuation by NFL Teams
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys reportedly remain in pursuit of a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., but it sounds like they're hesitant to meet his asking price.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys reportedly remain in pursuit of a trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., but it sounds like they're hesitant to meet his asking price.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano detailed Porter's trade market, with Fowler reporting that the Cowboys "have inquired about" trading for him, but "there was no movement as of Wednesday morning, and Dallas doesn't seem eager to relinquish major capital to secure Porter just yet."

Porter has missed the first three games of the 2026 season while recovering from a back injury and is listed as out for Thursday night's matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

Graziano reported that Porter's "unresolved contract situation still makes that uncertain." The 26-year-old reportedly rejected a contract extension that would have paid him slightly over $27 million for the 2026 season, and his contract demands could hurt his trade market.

"Dallas believes it could use Porter as a prolific boundary corner," Fowler explained. "Porter has a trade market, but his desire for a new contract -- and the rising costs of a position that's now well above $30 million per year -- complicates matters."

Graziano reported that "the consensus around the league seems to be that Porter is a good cornerback but not among the elites at the position." Teams that have inquired about trading for him "aren't willing to offer enough in return to convince the Steelers to part with Porter AND also sign him to the contract he wants." If he's hoping to be paid over $30 million per year, "it may be hard to find a team desperate enough to offer him that and the Steelers the compensation they're looking for."

The Cowboys and the other teams pursuing Porter will have to decide how much they're willing to give up to acquire him, and the Steelers could have to adjust their trade demands if they want to ship him away.

Porter, who has yet to make his 2026 debut, could potentially see the field Thursday when the Steelers take on the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: New Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Rumors on Jaguars' Asking Price, Potential Landing Spots
articles.summary: After a disappointing 2025 and a slow start so far in 2026, Brian Thomas Jr.'s future with the Jacksonville Jaguars is becoming a talking point around the NFL.
articles.body:
After a disappointing 2025 and a slow start so far in 2026, Brian Thomas Jr.'s future with the Jacksonville Jaguars is becoming a talking point around the NFL.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano , opposing clubs are "curious" to see what the Jaguars do with Thomas as teams start figuring out their needs leading up to the trade deadline.

Graziano noted it will probably take a "strong offer" to get the Jaguars to move Thomas, but he's a potential candidate to become available in the coming weeks.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

The Jaguars have been reluctant thus far to even really engage offers for Thomas. They reportedly turned down two "significant" trade proposals prior to the trade deadline last season.

There were strong reports about Thomas' performance and chemistry with Trevor Lawrence coming out of training camp, but that has not yet shown up in the regular season.

Thomas has just seven receptions for 88 yards with no touchdowns through three games (one start). He has played just 42.1 percent of the offensive snaps thus far, including under 40 percent in Weeks 1 and 3.

Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, both of whom have started all three games, are ahead of Thomas on the depth chart.

Since putting up 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, Thomas has 795 yards and two touchdowns in 17 games since the start of last season.

It could be argued the Jaguars would be better off exploring the market for Thomas right now. According to Graziano, he is still "perceived" as a No. 1 receiver based on talent but his strengths might not be a "great fit" with what Lawrence does well.

Graziano cited teams like the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers and Las Vegas Raiders among those that could have interest in Thomas if he becomes available.

Thomas is only 23 — he will turn 24 on Oct. 8 — and is under contract through the 2027 season. His fifth-year option for 2028 will have to be decided upon next spring.

The Jaguars are 15-5 since the start of the 2025 season, so they know their offense can succeed without Thomas playing at a high level.

articles.title: From $17 donations to $17 million: How Josh Allen turned his grandmother’s memory into a lasting legacy for children
articles.summary: Josh Allen’s charity story did not begin with a big fundraising campaign or a carefully planned foundation.
articles.body: Josh Allen’s charity story did not begin with a big fundraising campaign or a carefully planned foundation. It began with the loss of his grandmother and a simple gesture from Buffalo Bills fans. After Patricia Allen died in November 2020, thousands of fans began donating $17 to Oishei Children’s Hospital in her memory. What happened next turned a painful family moment into one of the most meaningful charitable efforts connected to an NFL player.How Patricia Allen’s memory became a mission to help childrenPatricia Allen was Josh Allen’s grandmother, and her death deeply affected the Buffalo Bills quarterback. Just days later, Allen played against the Seattle Seahawks and threw for 415 yards in Buffalo’s 44-34 victory.While Allen was dealing with his loss, Bills fans were finding their own way to show support. Many began donating $17 to Oishei Children’s Hospital because Allen wears No. 17.The donations came in from across the United States and other parts of the world. According to the Patricia Allen Fund’s official history, the donations passed $1 million by the end of 2020, with more than 30,000 people contributing. The donations came from all 50 states and 10 countries.The response was so strong that Oishei Children’s Hospital established the Patricia Allen Fund in December 2020 with input from Allen and his family. The purpose was to create something that could continue helping children long after the original donations were made.The fund supports the hospital’s pediatric critical care team, including the people who care for children in emergency rooms, trauma care and intensive care units. It also helps provide equipment, training and support for families going through difficult hospital stays.For Allen, this meant that his grandmother’s name would remain connected to something that could help other families.That idea became even more visible in November 2021, when the hospital unveiled the Patricia Allen Pediatric Recovery Wing. The playroom inside the wing was also named the Buffalo Bills Fans Fun Zone, recognizing the fans whose donations helped make the project possible.What started with people sending $17 had become something children could actually see and use.Josh Allen continued to put his own name behind the causeAllen could have simply thanked the fans and moved on. Instead, he continued supporting the hospital himself.In 2020, Allen donated $17,000 to the Patricia Allen Fund. He later partnered with Nike on another $100,000 donation to Oishei Children’s Hospital.He has also repeatedly used his position as one of the NFL’s most recognizable quarterbacks to bring attention to the cause.One of the biggest examples is the annual 117 Holes FOR Children’s Golf Marathon. The event began in May 2021 and has become a major fundraising tradition connected to the Patricia Allen Fund. The number 117 comes from Allen’s jersey number, giving the event the same personal connection that helped inspire the original fan donations.Allen has also taken part in fundraising efforts outside golf.In April 2022, he teamed up with Cash App for the Bitcoin Quarterback Challenge. Allen won the competition, and the event raised $700,000 for Oishei Children’s Hospital.Later that year, West Herr Auto Group made a $2,000,017 donation to the Patricia Allen Fund, which the hospital identifies as the largest single gift to the fund at that point.The fund has also benefited from other partnerships and campaigns. In 2023, Crosby’s donated more than $86,000 from a campaign, while EA Sports donated $10,000 to the fund after Allen was announced as the cover athlete for Madden NFL 24.The numbers tell one part of the story, but they do not fully explain why the charity has become so meaningful.The heart of it is still the same. Allen lost someone he loved, and a community decided to turn that sadness into something positive.Bills fans showed that the story was bigger than one teamPerhaps one of the most surprising chapters came from Kansas City.After the Bills lost to the Chiefs in the 2021-22 playoffs, Kansas City fans responded by donating to Oishei Children’s Hospital. They used $13 donations in reference to Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ jersey number.According to the Patricia Allen Fund’s official history, more than 17,000 Kansas City fans donated nearly $500,000 in February 2022.It was a remarkable moment because the donations came after a painful playoff loss for Buffalo.Rivalry usually means one side celebrates while the other side is disappointed. In this case, fans from the winning team found a way to recognize the person and the cause behind the losing team’s quarterback.That money went toward helping children who had nothing to do with football.It showed how far the original gesture had travelled.The Patricia Allen Fund reached another major milestone in 2026The Patricia Allen Fund continued to grow over the following years.In 2026, the fund reached the $17 million milestone after receiving support from more than 60,000 donors. The achievement showed that what began as a spontaneous response from Bills fans had developed into a long-term charitable effort with support from people far beyond Buffalo.For Allen, the timing carried another personal meaning.By 2026, he had also become a father. During his 117 Holes for Charity event, he spoke emotionally about how becoming a parent changed the way he understood the fear experienced by families whose children are seriously ill.Before becoming a father, Allen could understand those families through his experiences with children at the hospital and through the stories he heard. After having a child of his own, he said the situation felt different.He could imagine more clearly what it must feel like for a parent to sit beside a hospital bed and worry about their child.That perspective made an already personal charity feel even closer to home.A legacy that started with $17The Patricia Allen Fund is ultimately a story about how a small gesture can grow into something much larger.It started with fans giving $17 because they wanted to remember Josh Allen’s grandmother. Those donations became more than $1 million in the first few weeks and eventually grew into a fund that reached $17 million, supported by more than 60,000 donors.The money has helped support pediatric critical care, equipment, training and family programs at Oishei Children’s Hospital.But perhaps the most meaningful part is that the charity has never been only about a number.It is about children receiving care when they need it most. It is about parents trying to stay strong while their child is sick. It is about hospital workers having the equipment and support they need. And it is about keeping Patricia Allen’s memory connected to something that continues to help people.For Josh Allen, a painful loss became a reason to give back.For Bills fans, $17 became a way to show that they were standing beside their quarterback.And for thousands of children and families, that simple act of kindness has turned into real support when they need it most.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jayden Reed Injury Update, Packers WR's Timeline to Return After Surgery Decision
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed is scheduled to undergo neck surgery and will miss the rest of the season, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed is scheduled to undergo neck surgery and will miss the rest of the season, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.

LaFleur added that he doesn't believe this is a career-ending injury.

NFL insider James Palmer provided more insight:

Reed also posted on Instagram this morning: "God will use the unusual to do the unexpected… 11 out🙏🏾."

The fourth-year pro out of Michigan State initially suffered the neck injury in the Packers' 20-17 overtime road win over the New York Jets on Sunday, Sept. 20.

ESPN's Rob Demovsky explained what happened on the play.

"[Reed] was injured on the Packers' second play from scrimmage after he caught a 4-yard pass in the left flat. New York's Demario Davis turned Reed sideways with a tackle attempt and then fellow Jets defender Kingsley Enagbare caught Reed in the back/neck area with a glancing blow."

Reed's Packers teammates surrounded him as he was taken off the field on a stretcher.

Aneisha Cox, Reed's fiancée, provided an update on TikTok last week.

"Jayden is doing very good," Cox said. We greatly appreciate all the prayers and kind messages...It's 100 percent a day-by-day type of recovery."

Reed impressed in his 2023 rookie season, catching 64 passes for 793 yards and eight touchdowns. He followed that up with 55 receptions for 857 yards and six scores in 2024. Reed led the Packers in receiving both years.

Unfortunately, Reed was held to seven games in 2025 after suffering a broken collarbone in Week 2 against the Washington Commanders while making a diving touchdown catch on a play that was ultimately nullified due to a offensive holding penalty, per Demovsky . Reed also got surgery on a Jones fracture in his foot, an ailment he was playing through to start the season.

Reed came back for the final five games of the year (plus the Packers' Wild Card matchup). Last April, he and the Packers agreed to a three-year, $50 million extension ($20 million guaranteed).

This is a brutal blow for the Packers, who have certainly benefitted from Reed's playmaking abilities in the Jordan Love era. LaFleur spoke about Reed's absence, noting Skyy Moore will be in line for more targets in the passing game.

The Packers will look to get on track on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who are dealing with their own injury issues and will be without quarterback Baker Mayfield and wide receiver Jalen McMillan.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill Potentially Hints at NFL Landing Spot in Cryptic Social Media Post Amid Injury Rehab
articles.summary: Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill may have dropped a hint Wednesday regarding his next NFL destination.
articles.body:
Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill may have dropped a hint Wednesday regarding his next NFL destination.

In a post on X, Hill wrote, "I think I'm ready for some cold weather."

That post came just two days after Hill posted that it was "almost time to get off the couch and get to work."

The 32-year-old wideout suffered a torn ACL in late September last season while playing for the Miami Dolphins, and he went unsigned throughout the offseason as he rehabbed the injury.

Hill posted a workout video in July, and he said at the time that he had "no power" in his left leg:

However, Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, provided a much more positive update earlier this month.

During an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (h/t Kyle Dvorchak of NBC Sports), Rosenhaus noted that Hill was making progress and had multiple teams inquiring about his availability.

Rosenhaus also said that doctors recommended Hill should delay his on-field return until "perhaps some time in October."

Last week, Hill posted a workout clip on Instagram , and he appeared to show great explosion while running on the beach:

Considered one of the fastest and most electric wide receivers of his era, Hill has put up huge numbers and racked up numerous accolades over the course of his 10-year NFL career with the Kansas City Chiefs and Dolphins.

An eight-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and one-time Super Bowl champion, Hill has registered 819 receptions for 11,363 yards and 83 touchdowns in 145 career regular-season games.

While injuries limited him to four games last season, and he was banged up throughout the 2024 campaign as well, Hill isn't too far removed from a career year.

In 2024, Hill set career highs across the board with 119 catches for 1,799 yards and 13 touchdowns, earning him a second-place finish in the Offensive Player of the Year Award voting.

It is unclear if Hill can return to that level, but he has a chance to be a huge addition for whichever team signs him.

A return to Kansas City would potentially make sense for both parties, but there are plenty of other contending, receiver-needy teams who could possibly benefit from him as well, including the Baltimore Ravens, Las Vegas Raiders and Green Bay Packers, to name a few.

articles.title: NFL London games 2026: Jayden Daniels flies to London but status uncertain for Washington Commanders game at Tottenham
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels wears brace in practice but availability remains uncertain for Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium; watch live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm, followed by Los Angeles Rams against Philadelphia Eagles
articles.body:
Daniels dislocated his left elbow against the Dallas Cowboys in Week Two, but has flown over with the team ahead of Sunday's match-up against the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The former No 2 overall pick was absent in last weekend's victory over the Seattle Seahawks as veteran Marcus Mariota took the reins under center for his side's upset win over the Super Bowl champions.

Daniels wore a brace during a light jog-through on Wednesday, head coach Dan Quinn insistent he would not be rushed back.

"We won't put him out there before he's ready. That's why it's important to trust the process. But him being back on the field, that's a good step for us," Quinn told media.

Quinn explained it was "too early to call" if Daniels would be ready for Sunday's game, which marks the first of three games being played in London over the next month.

"As we get into Thursday and Friday, we'll see what that load looks like," he said. "By Friday we'll have a definite determination of where we're at. Until then, we'll work and start the process, but it would be too early to call."

Mariota went 19 of 31 passing for 183 yards and three touchdowns to lead Washington to a 33-31 win over Seattle in Week Three.

The Colts are meanwhile coming off a 19-17 win over the Houston Texans, Shane Steichen's side due to arrive in London two days later than their opponents.

Daniels had suffered the same injury in Week Nine last season before hurting it again five weeks later as he missed the final four outings of the campaign.

The same season also saw him miss time with knee and hamstring injuries, disrupting his efforts to build on an outstanding maiden campaign that culminated in him winning Offensive Rookie of the Year.

"His drive is always strong to return to play," Quinn said. "Any athlete would probably tell you when you're going through something a second time there's a known entity of what the road looks like. We all feel that way.

"He does know what that process looks like and the mobility and the strength. There's a known entity of when you're ready."

Sunday's matchup will represent the 43rd regular-season game to be played in the UK since 2007, but a new experience for Quinn.

"This is my first game as a coach in England and I'm pumped to be here," the Commanders head coach told reporters.

"People often ask me or the team, what's different about international games and you say travel or customs or the venue? But the thing I've want to emphasise with the team the most is what's exactly the same, and those are our anchors of what a Wednesday, a Thursday, and a Friday look like in terms of our preparation to get ready. And so that's a lot of the reason for coming early, so we can get back into that process. The quicker we get to that, less focus on what's different."

articles.title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Denies Rumors on Drake Maye Conflict Amid QB's Early Struggles
articles.summary: New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel talked about coming to Foxborough specifically because he wanted to coach Drake Maye when asked Wednesday about rumors regarding a potential split between himself and his starting quarterback.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel talked about coming to Foxborough specifically because he wanted to coach Drake Maye when asked Wednesday about rumors regarding a potential split between himself and his starting quarterback.

"Let me just tell you why I'm here. I'm here because Drake was the quarterback," Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "Believe it or not, I had choices to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here, because Drake was the quarterback.

"I don't have really much other to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source. But I'll just tell you what I've told numerous people if they want to ask me why I'm here."

The question Vrabel was answering concerned WEEI's Greg Hill saying on a recent radio show he had heard rumors of an "issue" between Vrabel and Maye, who has struggled during the Patriots' 1-2 start to the 2026 season.

Hill said on The Greg Hill Show he had heard from an "insider" that "despite what Mike Vrabel may have said publicly, it goes back to Drake Maye not being his guy."

The Patriots selected Maye with the No. 3 pick of the 2024 draft, then signed Vrabel to a multi-year deal as head coach ahead of the 2025 season.

Vrabel and Maye led the Patriots to a 14-3 record and a Super Bowl appearance in their first season together before struggling early in the 2026 campaign.

Maye has recorded just one total touchdown to go alongside six interceptions through the first three games of the campaign.

Vrabel referred to one of Maye's latest interceptions, an attempted throw to Efton Chism III that was picked off by Trevor Lawrence, as a "terrible decision" in his own appearance on The Greg Hill Show earlier this week.

"I'm confident that he'll continue to work. He'll continue to make, or begin to make, consistently better decisions," Vrabel said earlier this week about Maye.

Vrabel added, "You have to be counted on. There's pressure on all of us. This is professional sports."

Maye will get his next shot at redemption when the Patriots travel to New York this Sunday for a Week 4 matchup at the Buffalo Bills. The Bills are heading into the matchup with a 3-0 record but a passing defense that has allowed the sixth-most yards against in the NFL so far this season.

articles.title: CFB Insider Says Jim Harbaugh Will Get a 'Look' from Teams If Chargers Fire HC amid Struggles
articles.summary: Amid the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-3 start to the 2026 season, head coach Jim Harbaugh's job could be in jeopardy, but he reportedly has a fallback option if he hits the unemployment line.
articles.body:
Amid the Los Angeles Chargers' 0-3 start to the 2026 season, head coach Jim Harbaugh's job could be in jeopardy, but he reportedly has a fallback option if he hits the unemployment line.

Dan Wolken of Yahoo Sports spoke to an insider who revealed that Harbaugh could have the chance to return to college football if the Chargers part ways with him this season.

"If he gets fired and is available, somebody will look," the coaching search industry executive told Wolken. "It comes down to timing."

Harbaugh coached at Michigan from 2015 to 2023 and won a national championship in his final year with the team before jumping to the NFL to take the Chargers' head coaching position.

Despite his success with the Wolverines, his tenure ended controversially, as he faced multiple NCAA sanctions for recruiting violations and an illegal scouting scandal. He has a 10-year show-cause order that will run through August 2038, and if he were to accept another college football coaching job, he would be suspended for the first season of his return. Wolken noted that he would also be barred from communicating with his team during his suspension, as well as participating in any coaching activities "including but not limited to team travel, practice, video study, recruiting and team meetings."

While many would expect these penalties to hurt Habuagh's viability as a college football head coach, Wolken went on to explain that any college team that pursues him would likely overlook those infractions and find a way to work around them "either through litigation or a plan where an interim coach would be in charge for one year."

"He's a heck of a football coach," one power conference athletic director said of Harbaugh. "I'd certainly vet him."

For now, Harbaugh will be focused on trying to help the Chargers end their early-season skid. If things get worse and he hits the open market, the 62-year-old will have a lot of hurdles to clear before he's able to return to the collegiate ranks.

articles.title: Sean Payton's Response to OC Davis Webb, Broncos' Offensive Struggles Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton ceded playcalling duties this offseason to offensive coordinator Davis Webb.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton ceded playcalling duties this offseason to offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

Week 1 created cause for concern, as the Broncos amassed just 176 yards in a 31-10 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Payton preached patience, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , and that may prove beneficial.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

"The Broncos offense is slowly finding its footing after a sluggish Week 1, and how head coach Sean Payton handled that first week -- and his first-time playcaller, Davis Webb -- behind the scenes was crucial from a tone-setting standpoint. Payton can be harsh after wins, something he sees as a way to avoid complacency. But that 31-10 loss to Kansas City on 'Monday Night Football' required something else. The Broncos had produced nine first downs for 176 yards in Webb's debut.

"Payton, one of the league's best playcallers over decades who had relinquished duties to Webb over the offseason, did not sound thrilled during his halftime interview. But word is that Payton was highly supportive in meetings that following week, for both his coaching staff and his slow-starting team. 'He was awesome,' one source said. 'He never wavered.'

Denver's offense got off to a slow start in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and the Broncos fell behind 13-3 in the middle of the third quarter. However, Denver responded with 17 unanswered points (including a pair of fourth-quarter touchdowns) to win 20-13. Quarterback Bo Nix finished the game with 288 passing yards (Denver also ran for 104 yards).

The Los Angeles Rams then shut out the Broncos 16-0 in the first half last Sunday night. However, Denver offense scored three touchdowns (plus a pair of two-point conversions) in the second half of a thrilling 30-26 comeback win.

So the second halves have been promising in the last two games, leading to victories. The Broncos also haven't had an easy schedule, facing teams that are 5-1 outside their matchups with Denver.

We'll see how the Broncos do in their search for a third straight win on Sunday as they visit another tough team in the undefeated San Francisco 49ers.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Jokes Titans 'Shipped Me Out' in Video, Didn't Get Offer Before Ravens Contract
articles.summary: Derrick Henry says the Tennessee Titans did not offer him a new contract before he signed with the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the 2024 season.
articles.body:
Derrick Henry says the Tennessee Titans did not offer him a new contract before he signed with the Baltimore Ravens ahead of the 2024 season.

"They shipped me out," Henry told reporters before facing his former team this Sunday (h/t ESPN's Jamison Hensley). "No, I don't want to say it like that. It's always love. But no, they didn't offer nothing at all."

Henry continued, "It was bittersweet. I knew the writing was on the wall throughout that season, and they were ready to move on. Good things don't last forever, so it was time for me to find a new home."

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

Sunday's matchup will mark the first time the Ravens (2-1) and Titans (0-3) have met since Henry signed a two-year, $19 million deal worth up to $20 million with the Ravens in 2024.

Henry had hit free agency that offseason after leading the NFL with 280 carries and recording 1,167 rushing yards with 12 touchdowns in 17 games of a campaign in which the Titans went 6-11.

The Athletic's Dan Pompei reported after that season the Titans had worked out the framework of a potential deal that would have sent Henry to the Ravens ahead of the 2024 trade deadline.

According to Pompei, Henry played out his expiring contract with the Titans after some of the team's leaders shot down the proposed deal.

Henry still knew his time in Nashville was up by the end of that season, if his decision to thank fans for his time with the Titans after the team's 2023 regular season finale was any indication.

Henry ultimately ended up in Baltimore, where he has reset the ceiling for a running back over the age of 30.

After two strong campaigns to begin his Ravens career, Henry leads the NFL in carries (66) and rushing touchdowns (six) while recording 301 rushing yards through three games of his age-11 campaign.

The Titans, which rank 24th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed so far this season, will be tasked with finding a way to limit Henry when the Week 4 matchup kicks off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Baltimore.

articles.title: Jalon Daniels Drops Epic Quote on Mindset After Being Named Bucs QB1 Amid Baker Mayfield Injury
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels shared an insightful quote he learned during his University of Kansas tenure with reporters on Wednesday as he prepares for his first NFL start on Sunday vs. the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels shared an insightful quote he learned during his University of Kansas tenure with reporters on Wednesday as he prepares for his first NFL start on Sunday vs. the Green Bay Packers.

"You can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," Daniels said before offering further explanation.

"You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it...if the team's low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even, and if we're high, then I have to be able to be low to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even keel as possible, and I think being able to go out there and have that even-keel feel, the team around you feels that."

Daniels is QB1 until starting QB Baker Mayfield returns after dislocating his right (throwing) thumb. Head coach Todd Bowles told reporters that Mayfield will miss at least three weeks.

Daniels is therefore in line to start Sunday vs. Green Bay before a quick turnaround for a Thursday Night Football matchup at the Dallas Cowboys. The third game in that stretch is at home on Sunday, Oct. 18 vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers.

It's a crucial run for the 0-3 Buccaneers, who certainly don't want to see their season go up in smoke early on. The good news is that the NFC South hasn't gotten off to a positive start, either, with the Atlanta Falcons, Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints all sitting at 1-2.

So Daniels has a great opportunity here to keep Tampa Bay within reach of the NFC South lead. Based on his remarks, Daniels has the right mindset as he looks ahead to victories.

At the very least, he has plenty of collegiate experience to draw from thanks to his 45 starts at Kansas. Of course, this is his first NFL start, but Daniels knows how to take the temperature of a room and lead a football team.

Kickoff on Sunday is set for 1 p.m. ET at Raymond James Stadium.

articles.title: Marshawn Lynch Reveals Shocking Stat About His Physical Running Style in New Video
articles.summary: Running back Marshawn Lynch wasn't much fun to hit for opposing defenders during his NFL career. But the punishment he doled out was also being received.
articles.body:
Running back Marshawn Lynch wasn't much fun to hit for opposing defenders during his NFL career. But the punishment he doled out was also being received.

Lynch unveiled Wednesday during The Art of Ward podcast that the Seattle Seahawks monitored the impact he was taking during games with sensors in his shoulder pads and told him it was equivalent to being in seven car crashes per contest:

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

In a 2019 study , Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Rochester Medical Center studied the impacts of all contact to potential brain injuries. The study used "helmet accelerometers" that "measured linear and rotational acceleration during all practices and games, recording all contact that produced forces of 10 gs or greater. Astronauts on the space shuttle experienced 3 gs during lift-off. Race car drivers feel the effects of 6 gs, and car crashes can produce brief forces of more than 100 gs. The 38 NCAA Division III players experienced nearly 20,000 hits across all practices and games. Of those hits, the median force was around 25 gs, with half of the hits exceeding that amount."

So yes, playing football—especially for a position like running back, where elite players are generally getting 15-30 touches per game and getting hit on most of them, plus the impact from any blocking assignments—is basically a series of small car crashes. Lynch, at least, was more Hummer than Fiat.

articles.title: Veteran coach offers to help Jerry Jones with Cowboys’ struggling defense
articles.summary: Wink Martindale offers Jerry Jones help.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have received an unusual offer of help as their defense continues to struggle through the opening weeks of the 2026 NFL season.

Veteran defensive coach Wink Martindale suggested owner Jerry Jones could call him after Dallas' 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens . Martindale discussed the Cowboys' defensive situation on Talkin' Ball with Pat Leonard. He did not hold back when discussing coordinator Christian Parker.

"I don't want to be an a****le, but he's being outclassed right now," Martindale said. "So Jerry [Jones] can call me and I'll go help him. But I'm talking about helping the coordinator.

"It's like the end of the game calls. They were playing essentially one-rat with outside leverage against him, and they run, double in cuts, which is hard to defend when you're playing outside leverage and gave up that chunk pass, and Lamar [Jackson] was smart enough to call the timeout, and they got the field goal unit out there."

Dallas enters Week 4 with a 1-2 record after allowing 34 points to Baltimore in Brazil. The Cowboys also surrendered 28 points during their season-opening loss to the New York Giants .

The defensive problems extend beyond one game. Dallas has allowed at least 165 rushing yards in each of its first three contests.

Cowboys face structural problems on defense

Football – NFL – Baltimore Ravens v Dallas Cowboys – Estadio Maracana, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil – 2026 Dallas Cowboys' Dak Prescott in action with Baltimore Ravens' Trey Hendrickson REUTERS/Brian Snyder Credit: REUTERS (Reuters)

The Cowboys have also struggled to generate pressure. They entered the week with only two sacks, while their secondary had not recorded an interception.

Martindale's comments highlight the experience gap surrounding Dallas' defensive staff. Parker is in his first season as defensive coordinator after previously serving as Denver 's defensive backs coach. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is also experiencing his first season leading an NFL team. That combination leaves Dallas without an experienced former head coach on its current staff.

The lack of defensive consistency has become more concerning because Dallas invested heavily in its roster during the offseason. Injuries have also complicated Parker's task. Jalen Thompson , P.J. Locke and Jonathan Bullard are among defensive players who have missed time.

Still, the Ravens exposed issues that went beyond personnel. Baltimore repeatedly created rushing lanes and moved the ball enough to set up Tyler Loop 's winning 56-yard field goal. Dallas had opportunities to win after overcoming a 24-13 deficit. However, the defense could not prevent Lamar Jackson from finding Zay Flowers for a crucial 27-yard completion.

That play put Baltimore in position for the winning kick with one second remaining.

So, Martindale's offer reflects the pressure surrounding Dallas' defensive structure. The Cowboys need better communication, tackling and situational execution. The team now faces three road games in its next four contests. Dallas travels to Houston next Sunday with little margin for continued defensive mistakes.

Whether Martindale's offer leads anywhere remains unknown. The Cowboys, however, need answers immediately.

articles.title: One trade 49ers are unlikely to make in 2026
articles.summary: The 49ers appear content to keep Mac Jones on the roster as a high-value backup for Brock Purdy.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers could be wheeling and dealing this year. With major injuries at the defensive line and receiver, head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch might need to look around the league to shore up positions of need ahead of the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10.

However, one trade they likely won't make is with one of their own: Backup quarterback Mac Jones .

Quarterback injuries have piled up around the NFL this season, making Jones a hot commodity for teams desperate to keep their offense alive. But the 49ers aren't expected to cash in on Jones this year, according to NFL insiders Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler .

The reasons are simple: The 49ers value Jones as a reliable spot-starter if Brock Purdy gets injured again, and therefore have a high asking price in any trade for Jones.

"It would take real draft capital — perhaps a Day 2 pick — to get in the door on Jones," Fowler wrote. "Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level, but he also sat out seven games last season, with Jones filling in admirably. San Francisco could be there at the end if its aging roster holds up, so it makes little sense to deal Jones right now."

Jones earned his reputation in 2025. When Purdy went down with an injury for a couple of weeks, he kept San Francisco's season afloat. He completed a career-high 69.6% of his passes for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions, and Jones led the 49ers to a 5-3 record in his starts.

The Niners wanted a second-round pick for him this offseason but were happy to keep him as a backup. The downside is that Jones is an impending free agent, so San Francisco will likely lose him for nothing.

"The 49ers have said they aren't interested in dealing him, and I believe it would take a lot to change their minds," Graziano wrote. "But if someone gets desperate enough, who knows?"

articles.title: Deion Sanders reacts to Travis Hunter’s difficult start in the NFL
articles.summary: Deion Sanders questioned Travis Hunter’s Jaguars role before Hunter recorded his first NFL interception in Week 3.
articles.body:
Deion Sanders is questioning how Jacksonville is using Travis Hunter in his second season. Hunter entered 2026 seeking to remain a two-way contributor after a knee injury cut his rookie year short. Through 2 games, his offensive role had been reduced while most of his work came at cornerback.

Sanders said he does not know what happens behind the scenes in Jacksonville, but he knows Hunter's abilities well. His comments added another layer to the early-season discussion around the No. 2 pick. Hunter produced his first NFL interception in Week 3, leaving his season with limited offensive involvement and a clear defensive breakthrough.

Sanders is puzzled by Hunter's early role

Sanders discussed Hunter's usage on his CBS Colorado show after the Jaguars ' first 2 games. "I don't ask questions because I'm not there," Sanders said, adding, "I have no idea what's going on" when discussing the way Jacksonville has deployed his former player.

The comments followed a change from Hunter's college workload. At Colorado, Sanders used Hunter at receiver and cornerback. Hunter won the 2024 Heisman Trophy after starring on both sides of the ball, and Colorado's final 2024 season records credit him with 96 receptions for 1,258 yards and 15 touchdowns, plus 4 interceptions.

Sanders had already expressed frustration in May that Jacksonville had not contacted him for advice about Hunter's transition. He later pointed to Hunter's Heisman season as evidence of his two-way ability.

The Jaguars entered 2026 planning to use Hunter on both sides while increasing his defensive workload. General manager James Gladstone said Hunter was "set to play both sides" and expected an uptick in cornerback usage compared with his rookie season, when he played more snaps at receiver.

That shift was obvious through the first 2 games. NBC Sports reported that Hunter played 4 offensive snaps and 29 defensive snaps against Cleveland , then 6 offensive snaps and 37 defensive snaps against Denver . He had 1 reception for 8 yards across those 2 games.

The limited offensive role came after Hunter's rookie season ended with a knee injury. He played 7 games in 2025, recording 28 catches for 298 yards and 1 touchdown, while also making 15 tackles and breaking up 3 passes on defense.

Week 3 changed the conversation around Hunter

Hunter's role remained limited offensively against New England on Sept. 27, but his defensive impact became much more visible. In Jacksonville's 35-6 win, he recorded 4 tackles, defended 1 pass, and intercepted Drake Maye in the end zone near the end of the first half.

The interception was Hunter's first in the NFL and stopped a Patriots scoring opportunity on 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line. Jacksonville's official game account identified the play as one of the key moments in the victory, with Hunter adjusting in the air to make the catch.

The play also offered a clearer look at the versatility Jacksonville expected when it selected Hunter. While his offensive opportunities remained limited, his ability to affect the game as a defender gave him another way to contribute early in his second NFL season.

Fun fact: Travis Hunter became the fifth NFL player since 1999 to record at least 100 receiving yards, a receiving touchdown, and a pass defended in the same game when he posted 101 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Rams in 2025.

The two-way experiment remains complicated

Hunter's current numbers show why the Jaguars' approach has drawn attention. Through 3 games in 2026, he has 9 tackles, 2 passes defended and 1 interception on defense, but only 1 reception for 8 yards on offense.

Jacksonville traded up to draft Hunter second overall because of his unusual versatility. The Jaguars have kept him involved on both sides, but the snap distribution has changed significantly from college and his rookie season.

His knee injury interrupted his rookie year after 7 games, and Jacksonville entered 2026 intending to give him more work at cornerback. The early results show a defensive role producing tangible plays while his offensive involvement remains small.

Sanders' comments add to a larger discussion

Sanders' remarks are notable because he coached Hunter for 3 seasons across Jackson State and Colorado and was part of the environment in which Hunter developed into a full-time two-way player. His public comments have consistently emphasized Hunter's ability to contribute on both sides rather than settle into only 1 position.

Jacksonville, meanwhile, has maintained that Hunter is capable of playing both ways. The offseason plan called for increased defensive usage without removing him from the offense, unlike his rookie workload, which leaned more heavily toward receiver.

The Week 3 interception adds another dimension to the discussion. Hunter did not suddenly become a full-time offensive weapon, but he produced a high-impact defensive play in a dominant Jacksonville victory. Sanders' concern about the workload therefore exists alongside evidence that Hunter is beginning to make meaningful contributions in the role the Jaguars have prioritized.

Hunter's NFL story is still taking shape

Hunter's first 3 games of 2026 have produced a mixed statistical picture, but the context matters. He returned from a serious knee injury, entered a new season with a different workload balance and has already made a notable defensive play that was missing from his rookie stat line.

Jacksonville is 2-1 after wins over Cleveland and New England. Hunter has appeared in all 3 games and is a regular part of the defense. He has also seen time on offense, although his role there has been limited through the first 3 games.

Sanders' comments remain focused on what Hunter is capable of doing rather than on a definitive judgment about Jacksonville's plan. His frustration centers on a player known for doing everything at Colorado while Jacksonville shapes a more specialized NFL role.

Deion Sanders said he has "no idea what's going on" with Travis Hunter's usage after 2 games.

Hunter played 10 offensive snaps across the first 2 games while he worked primarily at cornerback.

He recorded his first NFL interception against New England in Week 3.

Hunter has 9 tackles, 2 passes defended and 1 interception through 3 2026 games.

Jacksonville has continued using Hunter on both sides despite the sharp shift toward defense.

articles.title: Seahawks predicted by CBS Sports to achieve major feat in 2026
articles.summary: The Seahawks come away with the Vince Lombardi Trophy at the end of the season after defeating a slew of tough opponents in their path.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have been projected by CBS Sports to win the Super Bowl this season, following a postseason path that will place them at the top of the field in the NFC.

Seattle is projected to secure the No. 1 overall seed in the NFC and earn a first-round bye in the playoffs. That position will give the Seahawks home-field advantage entering the divisional round, where they are forecasted to face the Los Angeles Rams .

Seattle defeats its NFC West rival 23-20 and advances to the NFC championship game to face the Detroit Lions . After downing Detroit 27-21, Seattle is projected to meet the Kansas City Chiefs in the Super Bowl. The forecast has the Seahawks defeating the Chiefs 20-19 to claim their second straight Vince Lombardi Trophy.

The scenario gives the Seahawks a challenging route to the Super Bowl despite having a first-round bye, beginning with a division opponent familiar with Seattle's personnel and style of play. The Lions have one of the most talented rosters on paper and present teams with a major test every week. A potential matchup with Kansas City on the NFL's biggest stage pits Sam Darnold and company against superstar QB Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs.

The Seahawks' projected road to the Lombardi Trophy highlights the expectations surrounding the team as it seeks to turn early-season momentum into a deep postseason run that culminates in a second straight Super Bowl win.
